- Table-hit samples only carve voxels more than TRUNC (12 mm) in front of the table surface. With the boards lying flat at k=0, the bottom ~12 mm of a ~2 cm slot gets no free-space update. The `--close fill/near` step can then fill it.
- This could explain a partial slot. Our 13.5 cm³ overlap is roughly 1/8 of the ≈105 cm³ that two unslotted boards would overlap if crossed over their full height. That figure is an estimate from our mesh extents.
- Status: hypothesis, not yet tested.

sources.title: Approximate Convex Decomposition for 3D Meshes with Collision-Aware Concavity and Tree Search (CoACD), plus its 2026 real-metric mode
sources.method: Cuts a mesh with 3D planes chosen by multi-step tree search until a collision-aware concavity falls below a threshold. The concavity is the shape-to-hull distance measured on both the boundary and the interior. The paper names 'filling a toaster's slots' as the failure of earlier decompositions that it is designed to avoid. Since 2026-04, real_metric=True takes the threshold in metres. That option is present in our installed coacd 1.0.11.
sources.solves_for_us:
Simulator side of problem 2:
- A correctly slotted board mostly survives Newton's default decomposition, but some hull material stays in the slot. That leaves residual overlap at the assembled pose even after the reconstruction is fixed.
- What to do: check overlap on the hull union, not on the mesh. Then add 1–2 mm of slot clearance, or use a lower or real-metric threshold.
- Problem 3: hull inflation of noisy undersides can also contribute to the 1–4 cm float.
sources.evidence:
Paper (abstract): decompositions are closer to the input with fewer parts on a large articulated-object dataset (no numbers in the abstract). Our work log: Newton runs CoACD with threshold 0.05 on every collision mesh.

Our synthetic CPU test (22.9×13×2 cm board, 2×6.5 cm through-slot):

| Setting | Hulls | Slot volume inside hulls | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| threshold 0.05 | 3 | 9.6% (~2.5 cm³) | 11 s |
| threshold 0.05, preprocess 'on' | 3 | 9.6% | 10 s |
| threshold 0.02 | 5 | 3.8% (~1 cm³) | 20 s |
| real_metric 3 mm | 5 | 3.8% | 18 s |
sources.code: https://github.com/SarahWeiii/CoACD (MIT); already in the FlashCHORD venv (coacd 1.0.11)
sources.adoption_effort: Hours, CPU only. Main risk: we may not control the decomposition the official evaluator applies to our submitted meshes.
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: SPARCS: Simulation-Ready Cluttered Scene Estimation via Physics-aware Joint Shape and Pose Optimization
sources.solves_for_us:
The principled form of our hand patches:
- A never-seen underside (the ep18 sweeper) becomes the plane that makes the observed rest an equilibrium.
- Non-penetration with the table and partner objects addresses floating (problem 3), ep24 board overlap and the cup in the rack.
- Limitation: it cannot create new concavities (slots), because hull topology is fixed by the initial decomposition.
sources.code: None yet: the project page (https://rory-weicheng.github.io/SPARCS/) says 'Code (To be released soon)'.
sources.rule_risk: Its SAM3D initialisation is a pretrained generative prior (grey zone). Initialising from our own TSDF meshes removes the conflict.

sources.title: PhysPose: Refining 6D Object Poses with Physical Constraints
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 3: objects floating 1–4 cm, and the cup tipping 23° in the rack. Also the pose side of ep24's assembled state. It works per rest interval against the table and the partner, using the same convex pieces the simulator collides. Pose only: it cannot fix a missing slot or a rounded underside.
sources.code: Not found. Project page: https://data.ciirc.cvut.cz/public/projects/2025PhysPose/
sources.adoption_effort: About 0.5–1 day on CPU. Reuse the CPU MuJoCo signed distances already used in pipeline/contact_retarget.py, add the gravity and support term, and run it per detected rest interval before mkref.
sources.rule_risk: None: uses only our meshes, tracks and table plane.

sources.title: Newton collision pipeline (SDF mesh-mesh and hydroelastic contacts) and Factory: Fast Contact for Robotic Assembly
sources.method: Newton can precompute an SDF per mesh (mesh.build_sdf) and generate contacts for concave mesh pairs from distance queries, optionally as hydroelastic patches. It can replace MuJoCo-Warp's convex-only contact generation through SolverMuJoCo(use_mujoco_contacts=False). Factory showed that SDF-based contact makes interlocking assembly (nuts and bolts) simulable at scale.
sources.solves_for_us: Simulator side of problem 2: the actual concave board meshes (slots, sharp edges) would collide instead of hulls. That removes the slot fill measured above and the hull inflation linked to problem 3.
sources.evidence:
- The docs say SolverMuJoCo's built-in pipeline 'handles convex primitive contacts', while Newton's pipeline enables 'SDF-based mesh-mesh contacts and hydroelastic contacts that MuJoCo's built-in pipeline does not support'.
- Our cached newton 1.2.0 ships examples/contacts/example_brick_stacking.py, which uses mesh.build_sdf + CollisionPipeline + SolverMuJoCo(use_mujoco_contacts=False), plus nut_bolt_sdf and nut_bolt_hydro examples.
- Factory (abstract): real-time or faster simulation including 1000 simultaneous nut-and-bolt interactions.
sources.code: Newton is already in the FlashCHORD venv (newton 1.2.0, licence not checked). Factory ships in Isaac Gym / IsaacLab.
sources.adoption_effort: 1–2 days to wire into the FlashCHORD scene build, plus a GPU test of memory and speed at 4096 worlds (unknown cost). Only worth it if the official evaluator also collides SDFs; otherwise training and evaluation would mismatch.
sources.rule_risk: None. The risk is an evaluator mismatch.

sources.title: MoreFusion: Multi-object Reasoning for 6D Pose Estimation from Volumetric Fusion
sources.method: Builds an object-level volumetric map of occupied and free space from multiple RGB-D views. Pose hypotheses are refined jointly by differentiable collision checking: an intersection loss between each object's voxelised model and the union of the other objects' occupancy and observed free space (ICC). ICP follows.
sources.solves_for_us: The 'others' occupancy and observed free space are forbidden' principle. Applied to geometry rather than only pose, it is the occupancy-arbitration rule for co-located pairs (ep24 boards, cup in rack, lid on pot). Our TSDF already carves with hands and other objects frame by frame; MoreFusion does it jointly for all objects at once.
sources.evidence: On YCB-Video and Cluttered YCB-Video, ICC+ICP gives the best AUC of ADD(-S) across visibility levels. ICC alone loses to ICP at visibility ≥40% because of its 32³ voxel discretisation (Fig. 9; values only in the plot).
sources.code: https://github.com/wkentaro/morefusion. Non-commercial Imperial licence (the LICENSE header reads 'DEEPFACTORS SOFTWARE LICENCE AGREEMENT'). Needs known CAD models.
sources.adoption_effort: Idea only, a few hours. The code assumes known models and has old dependencies.
sources.rule_risk: None for the idea.

sources.title: CAST: Component-Aligned 3D Scene Reconstruction from an RGB Image (physics-aware correction stage)
sources.method:
A relation graph (Stack, Lean, Hang, …) is reduced to Contact (bidirectional) and Support (unilateral) edges. Object poses are then optimised with SDF costs: no penetration plus at least one contact point per Contact edge, and only the supported object moves. For flat supports they regularise SDF values near the contact region so that partially reconstructed objects sit flush.

They deliberately do not settle the scene in a rigid simulator: initial penetrations destabilise the solver, too-fine convex decomposition gives non-flat surfaces and falls, and too-coarse decomposition gives floating.
sources.solves_for_us: A template for one generic 'contact graph → constraints' stage in place of per-object patches. Their stated failure reasons match ours: penetrating initial states, falls and floating caused by decomposition. We would build the graph from our tracks rather than GPT-4v.
sources.evidence: Evaluated by CLIP / GPT-4 rankings and a user study (visual quality, physical plausibility), plus 3D-Front CD / F-score / IoU. Physics gains are shown only qualitatively (a floating surfboard grounded, penetrating guitar and cooler separated).
sources.code: None found.
sources.adoption_effort: The correction stage can be reimplemented in hours (Open3D SDF + PyTorch, or our MuJoCo distances).
sources.rule_risk: Its object generator and GPT-4v are pretrained priors (grey zone). Use only the correction idea.

sources.title: Assemble Them All: Physics-Based Planning for Generalizable Assembly by Disassembly
sources.method: Starts from the assembled state and searches for disassembly motions using physics simulation (point-based SDF collision on DiffRedMax), pushing parts out. The assembly plan is the reverse.
sources.solves_for_us: A feasibility test for reconstructed mating geometry. If our slotted boards cannot be separated along the reverse of the tracked insertion path without penetration, the slot geometry or assembled pose is wrong. It also gives the insertion axis, which decides which board carries the top notch.
sources.evidence: State-of-the-art success rate and the highest efficiency against baselines on thousands of industrial assemblies. Solves 80-part assemblies within minutes and generalises to screws and puzzles (abstract).
sources.code: https://github.com/yunshengtian/Assemble-Them-All (MIT). Requires building their simulation bindings.
sources.adoption_effort: About 1 day with their code, or a few hours for a kinematic version: sweep board B along its tracked path in board A's frame and record MuJoCo penetration.
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: Beyond Point Clouds: Scene Understanding by Reasoning Geometry and Physics (Zheng et al.; IJCV 2015 extension)
sources.method: Labels voxels as empty, surface or invisible (occluded). Completes each segment into a solid primitive by filling invisible voxels in its occluded visual hull, under occlusion and solidity assumptions. Then groups primitives into objects that are stable under gravity, with a contact / support graph optimised by Swendsen-Wang cuts.
sources.solves_for_us: The classic statement of the missing half of our closing step. Invisible space may be filled, but the completed object must be stable at its observed rest. Our `--close fill` does only the first half; that is why ep18's underside came out rounded and unstable. It also supplies the support graph for S1.
sources.evidence: Better object segmentation, 3D volumetric recovery and scene parsing than baselines on a public and an own dataset (abstract; numbers not retrieved).
sources.code: None.
sources.adoption_effort: Idea only.
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: PolyFit: Polygonal Surface Reconstruction from Point Clouds (CGAL Polygonal Surface Reconstruction)
sources.method: Extracts planar primitives from the points, intersects them into candidate faces, then selects a watertight manifold subset by binary linear programming that trades off data fit, coverage and model complexity.
sources.solves_for_us: The rounded board edges in problem 2: our boards have no stable standing pose. It may also recover notch walls where their points were observed. Possibly the dust-pan and sweeper bases too. Sharp planar models replace the hand edits in library_v4. It is single-object and does not resolve mating by itself.
sources.evidence: CGAL docs and the paper claim it recovers sharp features and is robust to noise and outliers. Tested on multi-view stereo, Google Tango, laser and PrimeSense data.
sources.code: CGAL (GPL); standalone repo with old Qt/CGAL pins.
sources.adoption_effort: 1–2 days if the CGAL Python bindings cooperate. Fallback in hours: RANSAC planes plus a union-of-boxes fit for the boards.
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: PhyRecon: Physically Plausible Neural Scene Reconstruction
sources.method: Multi-view neural SDF plus a differentiable particle-based rigid simulator. Surface Points Marching Cubes turns the SDF into points so that stability losses (gravity, contact) backpropagate into geometry. Rendering and physical uncertainty down-weight bad monocular priors. Physics-guided pixel sampling targets slender structures.
sources.solves_for_us: Shows that physics losses can reshape hidden geometry inside reconstruction. Physics-guided sampling for thin parts is a possible idea for the dish rack. Too heavy for our timeline.
sources.evidence: At least 40% better physical stability (Isaac Gym) across all datasets, and better reconstruction quality (abstract).
sources.code: https://github.com/PhyRecon/PhyRecon (licence file not found). Needs torch 2.0.1 / cu118 and per-scene training.
sources.adoption_effort: Days of GPU work per scene setup. Not worth it within 13 days.
sources.rule_risk: Uses pretrained monocular normal and depth priors (grey zone).

sources.title: DemoBot: Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Third-Person Human Videos
sources.solves_for_us:
The closest system to ours, and evidence that the field supplies mating geometry through given models. Two transferable pieces:
- Constraint-based refinement of the assembled relative pose. For ep24: boards perpendicular, bottoms on the table plane, notch planes aligned.
- Success-gated or event rewards for the slotting phase.
sources.evidence: Real-robot multi-step assembly 12/20 (60%). Simulation ablations over 5 seeds show each component helps.
sources.code: Not found.
sources.adoption_effort: Idea only. The constraint refinement takes a few hours.
sources.rule_risk: Relies on given object models, which we may not use at eval. The pose-constraint idea itself is fine.

ideas: H1 (cause of ep24's missing slots; CPU, about 1 h). When the boards lie flat at k=0, slot voxels within TRUNC (12 mm) of the table get no free-space update, because table-hit samples only carve beyond TRUNC. `--close fill/near` then fills them. Fix: carve any voxel above the per-frame table plane that lies in front of an observed table or background point, with no truncation. Test: re-run recon_mesh on ep24 with this carve and measure the slot volume and the overlap of the two meshes at the assembled pose (now 13.5 cm³). Falsified if the overlap stays above 5 cm³, or if the slot voxels were already free before closing.

H2 (mask / visual-hull carving as a general S0 rule). A voxel that projects outside the object's 2D mask, at a pixel not occluded by a hand or another object, is free. This recovers every concavity visible in silhouette: the through-notches, the gaps between the dust-pan handle and its body, the rack openings. Test:
- per-object silhouette IoU on held-out public frames, and slot recovery on ep24;
- diagnostic only: registered mesh-vs-scan AUC for all 11 objects must not drop by more than 0.005.
Falsified if mask errors erode thin parts (rack wires, spoon) by more than that.

H3 (occupancy arbitration for co-located pairs, replacing per-object slot carving). At every rest where two objects overlap:
- Each overlap voxel goes to the object that observed it as inside.
- Voxels unobserved by both go by the swept volume. Voxels swept by B's observed-solid part along B's tracked path in A's frame during the last ~1 s before the rest are free for A, and vice versa.

This should give both cross-halving notches with the correct up/down side. Test, on ep24: assembled-pose overlap below 0.5 cm³, notch sides match the video, each board keeps ≥95% of its volume. On ep12 (cup in rack) and the pot/lid episodes: neither object loses more than 5% volume. Falsified if tracking noise of a few mm makes the carved notch more than 1.5× the partner's thickness, or flips its side.

H4 (simulator-geometry check, S4; CPU, a few hours). Our synthetic test shows Newton's CoACD at threshold 0.05 leaves 9.6% of a perfect 2 cm slot filled by hulls (about 2.5 cm³). Hypothesis: the overlap of the colliding hull unions at the mating pose, not mesh overlap, sets the assembled-state forces. Test: decompose our slotted boards exactly as FlashCHORD does, place them at the tracked assembled pose, and measure hull-union overlap and the 1 s settle drift in CPU MuJoCo. Then compare 1–2 mm slot clearance and real_metric 2–3 mm. Falsified if hull overlap is already below 0.5 cm³ and the pair settles within 3 mm / 3°.

H5 (SDF contacts for interlocking pairs). With Newton SDF mesh-mesh contacts (use_mujoco_contacts=False) a board seats in the partner's notch; with CoACD hulls it jams or pops. Test: CPU drop / insertion of B along its tracked last-second path in both modes, success being the final relative pose within 3 mm / 3° of the track; then 64 → 4096-world GPU memory and speed. Do not adopt unless the official evaluator also uses SDF contacts; falsified if hulls with clearance seat equally well.

H6 (physics-consistent rests, S3, generalising flatten_base and the stable-pose snap). Per rest interval:
1. Pose refinement in the PhysPose style: stay close to the track, no penetration with the table or partner, gravity / support term.
2. Then change only never-observed voxels (TSDF 'unknown'), replacing them with the support plane (table or partner) so the centre of mass lies over the support polygon (the SPARCS separating-plane idea).

Test on all public episodes: the fraction of rests that hold for 2 s in MuJoCo with no hand (drift below 5 mm, tilt below 2°) rises to ≥95%, and float drops below 2 mm. ep18 must stay at or above 0.70 and easy episodes (ep27 0.94) must not lose more than 0.01 AUC. Falsified if it is no better than the current flatten + snap.

H7 (cause of the 1–4 cm float). At reference frame 0 for ep12, ep24 and ep27, compare three heights: mesh minimum z, the minimum z of the CoACD hull union, and the table plane. If the hull–mesh gap explains more than 50% of the float, fix it in S4 (decomposition and clearance). Otherwise it is pose or perception error, and the H6 gravity term fixes it. Falsified if neither accounts for the float, which would point to table-plane error.

H9 (disassembly feasibility for slots). Kinematically sweep B along the reverse of its tracked insertion in A's frame and record penetration. Test: p95 penetration below 2 mm over the last 1 s of insertion for the reconstructed slotted boards. A failure means the slot width or depth, or the assembled pose, is wrong. Falsified as a useful check if it passes for unslotted boards as well, which would mean tracking noise dominates.

H10 (planar refit for planar objects). RANSAC planes + PolyFit, or a union-of-boxes fit, gives the boards sharp edges and a stable standing pose without hand edits. Test: each board stands on each long edge for 2 s in MuJoCo, and mesh-vs-scan registered AUC (diagnostic only) does not drop. Falsified if PolyFit fails to give a watertight result, or erases the notch, on our noisy points.

H11 (cross-halving constraint on the assembled pose, after DemoBot). In the assembled interval, project the two boards' relative pose onto a constraint set: board planes perpendicular, both bottoms on the table, notch walls coplanar. Test: the overlap and settle check from H4 improve and registered AUC on ep24 does not drop. Falsified if the constrained pose disagrees with the tracked one by more than 5 mm or 5° (tracking is then better than the prior).
gaps: Whether the official evaluator re-decomposes our submitted meshes with CoACD (Newton's threshold 0.05), uses separate collision meshes, or could use SDF contacts. This decides whether slot fidelity in the simulator is under our control at all.

Our 13.5 cm³ assembled overlap is about 1/8 of the ≈105 cm³ two unslotted boards would overlap if crossed over their full height. That figure is an estimate from our mesh extents (2.66–3.05 cm thick, ~13 cm tall). So either the meshes already carry partial slots (the H1 mechanism) or the tracked assembled pose is not fully seated. This is unresolved, and it decides which fix comes first.
I found no paper that recovers hidden mating geometry from observed relative motion (swept-volume carving between two tracked objects). H3 is our own untested hypothesis.
SPARCS code is not released and costs 46–540 CPU-minutes per scene. PhysPose code was not found. Only the ideas are transferable within 13 days.

Thin-wire objects (plastic_dish_rack) under 4 mm voxels and convex decomposition: no source found on preserving wire-frame containment geometry. The cup-tipping root cause (rack geometry vs pose) is not established.
The synthetic CoACD test used an exact box board with no rounding or noise, and trimesh reported the mesh as not watertight (volume correct). Our real reconstructed boards may decompose differently.

Real slot widths and clearances of the planter boards are unknown without the scans, which we may use for diagnostics only. Insertion with near-zero clearance in simulation may need force feedback or reward shaping (InsertAnything, arXiv 2609.24511, reports sim-only training down to 0.02 mm clearance on a robot arm, a different set-up).

PhyRecon, CAST, SPARCS and Agentic Real2Sim (arXiv 2607.19190) all lean on pretrained priors (monocular geometry, SAM3D, a generative object model, a VLM). Whether the organisers accept these is in the rules' grey zone and was not checked.

WebFetch could not resolve arxiv.org or newton-physics.github.io in this session. Primary pages were read with curl instead, and table values were pulled from MathML (SPARCS) or plots (MoreFusion, values not extracted).

verified.angle:
I fact-checked the multi-object-assembly survey: how published work recovers mating geometry and physically valid rests that sensors cannot see, and whether that work fits our pipeline (TSDF meshes, pinned FlashCHORD/Newton evaluator, CoACD hulls).

I opened the primary sources with curl: arXiv abstract and HTML full text (tables extracted), project pages, the CoACD README and licence, PyPI release dates, the Newton docs and the Newton licence. I checked them against our own verified notes (docs/professor-package/notes/19-collision-hulls.md, docs/work-log.md 2026-10-22 entries) and against pipeline/recon_mesh.py.

**Bottom line**
- The papers and numbers the colleague quotes are real and almost all stated correctly.
- Two recommendations do not fit our setup, because the evaluator is pinned:
  - a lower or real-metric CoACD threshold;
  - Newton SDF contacts.
- The cause attributed to problem 3 is contradicted by our own measurements.
- One closely relevant paper (Vysics, RSS 2025) was missed.

**Not done**
- I did not re-run the colleague's synthetic CoACD test: coacd is not installed in this sandbox, and I did not modify the environment.
- I could not use the GitHub API (repo access not enabled), so I checked repository licences through raw.githubusercontent.com where that worked.

checked.title: CoACD: Approximate Convex Decomposition with Collision-Aware Concavity and Tree Search (Wei, Liu, Ling, Su; SIGGRAPH 2022 journal track) + 2026-04 real-metric mode
checked.claim_checked: Collision-aware concavity measured on boundary and interior. Plane cutting with tree search. The 'toaster slots' failure is the motivation. MIT licence. real_metric since 2026-04, present in coacd 1.0.11. A lower or real-metric threshold reduces slot fill.
checked.verdict: partly (facts confirmed; the main recommendation is not applicable to evaluation)
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**Paper and code facts (all confirmed)**
- The abstract says verbatim that prior methods 'may fail to preserve fine-grained details (e.g., filling a toaster's slots)'.
- The method:
  - a collision-aware concavity measured from both the boundary and the interior;
  - direct cutting with 3D planes, giving intersection-free hulls;
  - a multi-step tree search.
- The abstract has no numbers.
- README: '[News (2026-04)] CoACD now supports real metric mode (-rm)'; the API is `run_coacd(mesh, threshold=0.01, real_metric=True)`.
- README defaults: threshold 0.05, preprocess 'auto'.
- LICENSE: MIT (2022, Xinyue Wei, Minghua Liu).
- PyPI: 1.0.10 was released 2026-04-10, 1.0.11 on 2026-05-04 and 1.0.14 on 2026-08-28. 1.0.11 having real_metric is therefore consistent; our note 19 A17 also verifies this in the source.

**What the colleague misses, from our own verified notes (note 19)**
- Stage A table and A17: the pinned evaluator always calls `coacd.run_coacd(threshold=0.05, max_convex_hull=-1, preprocess_mode='auto')`. The call is 'not configurable', and FlashCHORD never passes real_metric. A lower or real-metric threshold is therefore not available at evaluation.
- The same notes (§1 item 1; A3, A14, A15) verify the actual lever:
  - every `<collision>` element is decomposed on its own;
  - URDF primitives (box, cylinder, capsule, sphere) are never decomposed;
  - a welded, closed, convex piece comes back from CoACD unchanged (0.000 mm), with ≤64 hull vertices because of MuJoCo's maxhullvert cap.
- The tolerance law (A17) is: hull ≤ 0.025·L from the mesh, with L the longest bounding-box extent. For a 23 cm board that is ≈5.7 mm.
  - The colleague's 9.6% slot fill (≈2.5 cm³) at 0.05 and 3.8% at 0.02 / 3 mm real-metric are consistent with this law.
  - I did not re-run them (coacd is not installed here).
checked.applicability:
The concern is right, but the fix is wrong.
- Do not plan on threshold changes. Author the collision geometry ourselves, so CoACD passes it through unchanged:
  - each board as about 3 URDF boxes (two legs plus a bridge), leaving the notch as an exact gap;
  - or as welded convex pieces.
- This also gives sharp, flat edges, so a board can stand on its edge.
- Check overlap on the pass-through pieces at the assembled pose.
- Keep the visual (scored) mesh separate. docs/research/novelty-2026-10-22.md already proposes collision-only edits so that registered AUC is unchanged. Whether organisers accept hand-authored collision geometry is open: note 19 §4 question (a) has been drafted, and I could not tell whether it has been answered.

**The colleague's float claim is wrong in sign.** They say 'hull inflation of noisy undersides can also contribute to the 1–4 cm float'.
- CoACD hulls are supersets of the mesh, so inflation pushes an object into the table, causing ejection or pop-up, not floating.
- Our measured drops (ep12 rack 1.07 cm in the assist-off drop test) are gaps in the simulated hulls themselves.
checked.code_status: MIT. coacd 1.0.11 is pinned by FlashCHORD; 1.0.12–1.0.14 exist but are not what the evaluator runs. The synthetic test script is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/scripts/slot_coacd.py; I read it but did not re-run it.

checked.title: SPARCS: Simulation-Ready Cluttered Scene Estimation via Physics-aware Joint Shape and Pose Optimization (Huang, Han, Ye, Pan, Hauser; RSS 2026, arXiv 2602.20150v3)
checked.claim_checked: The method (union of convex hulls; ALM + Levenberg–Marquardt; trimmed-ICP fit; equilibrium with friction; SDRS separating-plane collision potential; separating-plane aggregation regularising occluded contact regions; SAM3D + FoundationPose initialisation), its numbers (drift 0.73–3.10 cm vs 31–173 cm; KE 7e-4–1.1e-2 J vs 2.1–5.7 J; PSNR ≈17–22 dB; 46–540 min CPU) and its code status.
checked.verdict: confirmed (numbers and method); partly (interpretation for us)
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**Numbers (all confirmed from Tables I–III)**
- Max drift over 1 min: 1.62 / 0.83 / 3.10 / 0.73 / 2.28 cm, vs SAM3D 59.41 / 87.56 / 31.06 / 172.55 / 51.69 cm.
- Max kinetic energy in 1 s: 7.19e-4 to 1.12e-2 J, vs 2.08 to 5.73 J.
- PSNR: 17.92–21.43 dB.
- Wall time: 46.1 / 259.7 / 224.2 / 202.15 / 539.92 min. Scenes have 6–22 hulls; computation is on CPU, except texture.

**Method (confirmed)**
- Shapes are unions of convex hulls whose vertices are decision variables.
- Augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) with Levenberg–Marquardt subproblems.
- SDRS separating-plane barrier potential.
- Quasistatic force equilibrium with friction coefficient η = 1.
- Separating-plane aggregation (App. A-B): one plane per interacting object pair. The paper says this 'regularizes occluded contact regions by encouraging them to align with a common separating plane'. The colleague's paraphrase is fair.

**Details the colleague omits that matter for us**
1. The input is a single RGB-D image of a static scene.
2. Unseen regions are governed not only by physics: a Type III term pulls the hulls toward the SAM3D-hallucinated mesh (w3 = 0.02).
3. SDRS is an interior-point method and needs a strictly penetration-free start. They shrink each colliding pair by an SDF offset −δ until it is free.
4. With aggregation, SDRS 'implicitly treats each shape as its convex hull' for that pair. So aggregation cannot represent nested or interlocked pairs: cup in rack, lid on pot, the X boards.
5. Each object is limited to at most 5 hulls of at most 50 vertices (CoACD threshold 0.05).
6. Validation uses non-default MuJoCo settings: 1 ms timestep, implicit integrator, noslip 10, multi-CCD, elliptic cone, condim 4. Our evaluator runs 200 Hz with its own settings.
7. Mass is set by hand (800 kg/m³).

**Code**: the project page still says 'Code (To be released soon)'. A web search found no repository.
checked.applicability:
Too slow and too SAM3D-dependent to adopt. It covers one static scene per run, while we have many rest intervals per episode.

**What carries over**
- The principle: equilibrium plus non-penetration acting on unobserved geometry.
- The support-contact case: one plane per object–table pair, which is our flatten_base generalised.

**The colleague's 'cannot create slots' limitation is right**, but the stronger reason is item 3: our assembled ep24 boards overlap by 13.5 cm³, so SPARCS could only start after shrinking both boards. It is also unusable for interlocked pairs whenever aggregation is on.

A drift of up to 3.1 cm per minute in a tuned MuJoCo is not 'negligible' at ADD-AUC's 1–9 cm bins. Note 19 C7 also measures 5–11 mm drift in a 1 s hands-free settle, even for floor-level colliders.

**Rule risk**: dropping SAM3D also removes the only shape prior on unseen regions, leaving our TSDF guess there. A light variant must down-weight the fit term on unobserved voxels.
checked.code_status: Not released (project page checked 2026-10-22). Website licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

checked.title: PhysPose: Refining 6D Object Poses with Physical Constraints (Malenický, Cífka, Fourmy, Montaut, Carpentier, Sivic, Petrik; arXiv 2503.23587)
checked.claim_checked: Pose, collision and gravity costs. Collision as a hinge on convex-piece signed distance (DiffCol). Gravity switched off on contact. Table from two views with MASt3R + RANSAC. YCB-V average recall gains and ablation. Improved pick-and-place. No code.
checked.verdict: confirmed (minor rounding); applicability narrower than stated
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**Method (confirmed)**
- Pose cost: a Mahalanobis distance to the initial pose, with variance elongated along the camera ray.
- Collision cost: a hinge on negative signed distance between convex parts. The parts come from CoACD (ref [45] is Wei et al. 2022), and the differentiable GJK builds on DiffCol.
- Gravity cost: the average positive distance of each convex part to the nearest static part along gravity, disabled when the object 'is in collision with any other object'.
- Table plane: MASt3R on two views, metric scale from SuperGlue correspondences plus RANSAC, GroundingDINO for the table box, then a RANSAC plane fit.

**Numbers**
- YCB-V AR, Table 1: MegaPose 0.620 → 0.707, FoundPose 0.690 → 0.775. Table 2 row e gives 0.706 / 0.774, the colleague's figures; the paper is internally inconsistent by 0.001.
- With a support view: 0.650 / 0.715. Single view: 0.597 / 0.658. Known gravity: 0.648 / 0.710.
- Ablation on 10% of YCB-V: all terms 0.691; without pose 0.540; without collision 0.607; without gravity 0.615; no terms 0.611.
- HOPE-Video also improves: 0.353 → 0.395 and 0.286 → 0.324.
- The gains are in MSSD and VSD, i.e. depth; MSPD barely moves.

**Robot test**: 3 objects × 5 trials. Baseline success 0/5, 3/5 and 0/5; with PhysPose, 80% on all three. The sample is very small.

**Failure mode stated**: large initial collisions can flip the depth order of objects.

**Code**: none found. The project page has only arXiv and supplementary links; a web search found no repository.
checked.applicability:
Useful but limited. It moves only poses, and its gravity term is a 'move down until touching' pull with no torque or support-polygon test.
- It cannot stop the ep18 sweeper falling (centre of mass 3 cm outside a 0.3 cm² footprint).
- It cannot stop a cup tipping: gravity switches off as soon as the cup touches the rack.

Our measured data narrows its role further:
- ep12's 23° cup tip was mostly the rack dropping 1.07 cm. contact_retarget --rest_settle 1 already reduced it to 0.4 cm / 3.5° (work-log 2026-10-22, 06:40 TRT).
- Note 19 §1 item 7 measured, with the public assets, a 1 s cup-on-rack tilt of 24° falling to 2–3° once the rack collision mesh is split or welded. The residual is therefore a collision-asset effect, not a pose effect.
- The ep24 'float' is a perception bias: tracked z 2–2.5 cm too high while a board is static, compared with mocap after inference (work-log 03:20 TRT).

Adopt the one piece rest_settle lacks: object-on-object collision and support between our own hulls, run per rest interval. That is about 0.5 day on CPU.

Rule risk: none if we use our table plane from stereo (our table plane is metric already; MASt3R is not needed).
checked.code_status: No public code found (project page and web search, 2026-10-22).

checked.title: Newton collision docs (SDF mesh-mesh / hydroelastic contacts, use_mujoco_contacts) + Factory (Narang et al., RSS 2022)
checked.claim_checked: SolverMuJoCo's built-in pipeline handles only convex primitive contacts. Newton's pipeline adds SDF mesh-mesh and hydroelastic contacts through use_mujoco_contacts=False and mesh.build_sdf. This would remove slot fill and hull inflation. Factory simulates 1000 nut-and-bolt pairs in real time.
checked.verdict: confirmed (quotes); not applicable to our submission
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**Docs (latest version) say verbatim**
- SolverMuJoCo 'ships with its own built-in collision pipeline that handles convex primitive contacts'.
- Newton's pipeline enables 'SDF-based mesh-mesh contacts and hydroelastic contacts that MuJoCo's built-in pipeline does not support'.
- The examples it names are example_nut_bolt_hydro.py and example_nut_bolt_sdf.py.
- The shape table says a MESH shape is 'arbitrary, including non-convex; SolverMuJoCo collides its convex hull'.
- approximate_meshes supports convex_hull (default), bounding_box, bounding_sphere, coacd and vhacd.

**Licence**: Newton main branch LICENSE.md is Apache-2.0.

**Factory abstract**: 'real-time or faster simulation ... including simultaneous simulation of 1000 nut-and-bolt interactions'; 60 part models, 3 environments, 7 controllers.

**Caveat**: these are the latest docs; our pin is newton 1.2.0, so details may differ.
checked.applicability:
Our own notes have already answered the colleague's open condition ('only worth it if the official evaluator also collides SDFs'), and the answer is no.
- Note 19 C1 and C26 (verified against the code): the pinned FlashCHORD runtime/sim.py runs SolverMuJoCo with use_mujoco_contacts=True at 200 Hz.
- Every object mesh reaches MuJoCo as CoACD hulls, each capped by MuJoCo to ≤64 vertices.
- Switching to Newton contacts is a physics-config change, and it 'drops the geom contact parameters needed for grasping (sim.py:37-38)'.

Training on SDF contacts would therefore create a train/eval mismatch, and the evaluated physics would still use hulls. I would drop this from the plan; at most use SDF contacts offline as a reference.

The 'MESH collides as its convex hull' line also means a raw, undecomposed board mesh would lose its slot entirely. That reinforces authoring the collision pieces ourselves.
checked.code_status: Newton Apache-2.0, already installed (1.2.0). Factory ships in IsaacGymEnvs / IsaacLab; not checked further.

checked.title: Missed source: Vysics: Object Reconstruction Under Occlusion by Fusing Vision and Contact-Rich Physics (Bianchini, Zhu, Sun, Jiang, Taylor, Posa; RSS 2025, arXiv 2504.18719)
checked.claim_checked: The colleague wrote: 'I found no paper that reconstructs a hidden notch or slot from observation.'
checked.verdict: partly. No slot reconstruction, but there is direct prior work on inferring hidden contact geometry from observed motion. Only the abstract was checked.
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**Abstract (checked)**
- The input is a seconds-long RGB-D video plus robot proprioception, for a single rigid body.
- BundleSDF gives the trajectory and the visible geometry.
- The Physics Learning Library (PLL) infers 'physible geometry' through implicit contact-dynamics optimisation, i.e. the geometry that best explains the observed motion.
- Visible and physible geometry together fit one SDF.
- No pretraining and no tactile or force sensing.
- Reported to be more accurate than vision-only methods under heavy occlusion.

**Code**: the project page links github.com/DAIRLab/vysics. I could not read the repository or its licence (raw LICENSE/README returned 404; GitHub API access not enabled).

SPARCS also cites it, as Vysics ref [8], and cites an IROS 2012 'Inferring 3d shapes of unknown rigid objects in clutter through inverse physics reasoning'.
checked.applicability:
This is the closest published analogue to building meshes from how objects interact.
- Where Vysics has robot proprioception, we have MANO fingertips plus a known table plane.
- Hypothesis: frames where a tracked object pivots or slides on the table locate its hidden support points.
- Falsifier: on public episodes, after inference, the inferred support points should lie within about 5 mm of the scan underside.
- Running the full method is probably too heavy for 13 days. Read it before designing S3.
- Rule risk: none, since no pretraining is used.

checked.title: Spot checks: DemoBot (arXiv 2601.01651) and Combinative Matching (arXiv 2508.09780, ICCV 2025)
checked.claim_checked: Assembly-from-video work takes object models as given; 'opposite volume occupancy' is a principle learned on fracture data.
checked.verdict: confirmed
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**DemoBot**

checked.title: Colleague's in-repo claims: recon_mesh.py table-band carving, and the 'float' cause
checked.claim_checked: Table-hit samples carve only voxels more than TRUNC (12 mm) in front of the table, which could leave a partial slot. Hull inflation contributes to the 1–4 cm float.
checked.verdict: carving claim confirmed in code (still an untested hypothesis); float-cause claim not supported
checked.what_source_actually_says:
**Carving (recon_mesh.py)**
- Line 184 (`keep = ~other | (sdf > a.trunc)`) drops table, hand and other-object samples within ±TRUNC; trunc defaults to 0.012.
- Lines 158–164 carve below the table only beyond --below_carve (4 mm).
- So a band from about −4 mm to +12 mm around the table gets no free-space vote from table-hit rays, as the colleague says.

**Float cause (work log, 03:20 TRT)**
- Static boards sit 2–2.5 cm too high in our reference relative to frame 0, compared with mocap after inference.
- The lowest collision point is 3.6–4.5 cm (standing board) or 1–2 cm (flat board) above the table.
- After rest settling, board 1 is −1.5 cm, because 'our board mesh is narrower than the real board'.
- That is tracking bias plus mesh-size error, not hull inflation, which would point the other way.
checked.applicability:
**The float should be fixed at perception**: a table-contact prior during tracking for static objects. Diagnostic: the height of the lowest point above the table per rest interval, across all public episodes, against mocap after inference.

**The TSDF band hypothesis** is testable on CPU. Re-run recon_mesh on ep24 with table-hit samples allowed to carve down to the table plane, then measure:
- notch depth versus the scan (diagnostic only);
- the assembled-pose overlap, compared with 13.5 cm³.

corrected_ideas: Split every fix by where it acts. The scored mesh is the visual mesh, registered to the scans for ADD-AUC. The simulated geometry is our URDF `<collision>` elements, which the pinned evaluator decomposes with a fixed CoACD call. Because the call is fixed but primitives and closed convex pieces pass through unchanged (note 19 A3/A14/A15), the eval-compatible fix for slots, sharp standing edges and flat bases is authoring collision geometry ourselves. Example: each ep24 board as 3 boxes with the notch as an exact gap. The visual mesh stays as reconstructed, so registered AUC does not change. Flag: organisers have not confirmed that collision geometry may differ from the submitted mesh (note 19 §4 (a), docs/research/novelty-2026-10-22.md).

Drop two items from S4/S5: 'use a lower or real-metric CoACD threshold' and 'switch to Newton SDF contacts'. Both change the evaluator's fixed physics configuration (note 19 C1/C26: use_mujoco_contacts=True, CoACD threshold 0.05, hulls capped at 64 vertices), so they would create a train/eval mismatch. Keep SDF contacts only as an offline reference.

Restate problem 3 with measured causes. The ep24 boards float because our tracked z is 2–2.5 cm too high while they are static, and because our mesh size is off. This is not hull inflation, which would push objects into the table rather than float them. The ep12 cup tip was mainly the rack dropping 1.07 cm and is already 3.5° with rest_settle. The research target is therefore perception: stereo/track bias for resting objects and a table-contact prior in tracking. Falsifier: on public episodes, the per-rest lowest-point height above the table falls below 5 mm compared with mocap, checked after inference.

Make S3 a generic support rule that is not keyed to object or episode. Detect a rest from our tracks (no fingertip within 3 cm, static for at least N frames). Then require the convex support polygon of the collision geometry in contact with the table to contain the projected centre of mass, editing only voxels the TSDF never observed within a few mm of the table plane at that pose. This is SPARCS's support-plane idea without SAM3D or ALM. Verify with a 1–2 s no-hand settle in the evaluator's physics (MuJoCo, 200 Hz, our collision pieces) at every rest of every object in the 12 two-object public episodes. Falsifier: drift above about 5 mm or 5°, or registered AUC dropping by more than 0.01, on any public episode.

Extend rest_settle with PhysPose's missing piece: object-on-object support and non-penetration between our own collision pieces per rest interval (about 0.5 day CPU). PhysPose's gravity term has no torque or stability test, so it will not fix tipping. Do not expect it to fix the sweeper or the cup.

S2 occupancy arbitration for co-located static pairs: when two tracked objects keep a constant relative pose for at least N frames and their collision geometry overlaps, assign each overlap voxel to the object in which it was observed inside from an unoccluded view. Split voxels unobserved in both along the tracked insertion direction; this is still a hypothesis, and I found no paper that does it. For ep24 that means a notch from the top in one board and from the bottom in the other. Add clearance: the public GT boards show 1.6–3.2 mm (note 19 §4). Using about 2 mm is a development-derived constant, not eval tuning. Falsifier: collision-piece overlap at the assembled pose = 0 and a 2 s no-hand settle of the X stays within about 5 mm.

Before S2, test the colleague's TSDF hypothesis on CPU. Re-run recon_mesh on ep24 with table-hit samples allowed to carve down to the table plane (now they keep no vote within ±12 mm, recon_mesh.py:184), and see how much of the 13.5 cm³ overlap disappears. Only the notch depth versus the scan is a diagnostic after inference.

Read Vysics (RSS 2025) before designing S3. It infers hidden contact geometry from observed object motion plus contact dynamics, the closest published analogue to 'meshes from how pieces interact'. A cheap variant for us: frames where an object pivots or slides on the table locate its hidden support points. Falsifier: inferred support points within about 5 mm of the scan underside on public episodes (diagnostic only).

Do not reimplement SPARCS. It runs 46–540 CPU minutes per static single-view scene and leans on SAM3D for unseen regions (the grey zone). It needs a penetration-free start, and its per-pair separating-plane aggregation treats each object as its convex hull, so it cannot hold nested or interlocked pairs. Borrow only the support-plane regulariser (S3 above) and the shrink-to-feasible initialisation idea.

Keep the collision piece count small. Note 19 measured 760–1,340 contacts at reset and about 10x step cost when both partners are finely split, plus a CoACD debris-hull build-crash risk (about 1 in 2,100 hulls). Prefer a few primitives or convex pieces per object over fine CoACD splits, and screen every shipped piece on Linux.

found.angle:
Real-to-sim collision modelling: how real2sim pipelines get collision geometry, mass properties and automated sim-validity checks right, applied to our measured failures. These are a rounded unseen underside (ep18), boards with rounded edges and no slots (ep24), objects floating 1-4 cm (ep12/24/27), and a cup tipping in the rack (ep12).

Bottom line: the literature does not patch individual objects. It (a) restricts collision geometry to clean primitives or CAD-like surfaces that the simulator's convex decomposition keeps intact (CRISP; CoACD design), (b) treats the support and contact relations seen in the data as constraints on shape and pose together (SPARCS, PhysPose, PhyRecon, Atlas3D, CRISP contact-guided completion), and (c) checks what the engine actually collides with, using drop/settle tests (I2CD, PhyRecon, SPARCS, Atlas3D).

My own CPU measurement (coacd 1.0.11, scratchpad, synthetic boards 23x13x1.2 cm with cross-halving notches, assembled as an X):
- Sharp-edged CAD-like boards: CoACD at FlashCHORD's threshold 0.05 gives 3-4 hulls and keeps the slot open. Notch fill is 0 %, hull overlap 0.00-0.08 cm^3. Thresholds 0.02 and 3 mm real-metric give the same result.
- Without slots, overlap is 18.7 cm^3 (we measured 13.5 cm^3 on ours).
- The same boards made TSDF-like (2.5 mm voxels, Taubin smoothing, 0.7 mm noise): exact-mesh overlap is 0.81 cm^3, but the CoACD hull overlap is 6.9-7.1 cm^3 (two seeds). Forced manifold preprocessing raises it to 15.4-25.2 cm^3. Threshold 0.02 brings it down to 2.5 cm^3 but needs 29-33 hulls.
- So the threshold is not the main lever, and we cannot change it for the evaluation anyway. Getting the evaluated collision right means giving the evaluator's CoACD a clean, flat-faced, sharp-edged mesh.
- From CoACD's source: the normalised threshold t equals t·L/1.6 in metres. At t=0.05 that is about 7 mm for a 23 cm board, about 4.6 mm for the 14.7 cm sweeper and about 9-12 mm for a 30-40 cm rack.

Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/scripts/slot_coacd.py, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/scripts/slot_coacd_noisy.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/scripts/slot_run2.py (venv in the same scratchpad).

Proposed robust stages (a hypothesis for the owner):
- S1. TSDF reconstruction plus a per-voxel observed/unobserved confidence map.
- S2. Refit by shape class, editing only unobserved geometry: planar/extruded for the boards and the dust-pan plate; surface of revolution with a flat base for the cups, pot, lid and pitcher; thin primitives for the rack wires.
- S3. Constraints from interactions, collected over every frame: carve wherever another rigid body or the table is, and complete the support plane in each rest interval with the centre of mass over the footprint.
- S4. Per-frame refinement of object poses: gravity + non-penetration + staying close to the perceived pose.
- S5. A GT-free QA gate on the exact evaluator collision (FlashCHORD's CoACD): engine round-trip, rest and settle tests, penetration, floating, pair settle, perturbation.
- S6. GPU training and evaluation only after the gates pass.

sources.title: CoACD: Approximate Convex Decomposition for 3D Meshes with Collision-Aware Concavity and Tree Search (paper, README, source)
sources.method: Concavity metric that compares a shape with its convex hull at both the boundary and the interior. The mesh is cut directly with planes chosen by a multi-step tree search, so no voxelisation is involved. Options: threshold -t (0.01-1, default 0.05; normalised, about t·L/1.6 m by the source's real-metric conversion); manifold preprocessing -pm auto/on/off with resolution -pr 20-100 (default 50); merge; max hulls; extrude; real-metric -rm (threshold in metres); seed.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 2 (ep24 slots), and the dish rack and cup for problem 3. The evaluator collides our objects as CoACD hulls (threshold 0.05, settings fixed by FlashCHORD per our dissection), so the mesh we hand it must survive this exact decomposition. The CoACD paper says V-HACD-style volume metrics 'stuff the slots of a toaster', while CoACD keeps them when the slots are in the mesh. My measurement: with a clean notch the slot stays open; on a TSDF-like rounded, noisy surface the hulls bridge it.
sources.evidence: Paper Table 1: fewer components than V-HACD/HACD at matched concavity; my reading of the extracted table is about 20 vs about 45 components on PartNet-Mobility. Paper text: V-HACD fills toaster slots, rings and kettle spouts. My measurement (coacd 1.0.11, CPU, about 2 s per board): CAD-like slotted boards give hull overlap 0.00-0.08 cm^3 and 0 % notch fill at t=0.05, 0.02 and 0.003 m real-metric. TSDF-like boards give 6.9-7.1 cm^3 (auto), 15.4-25.2 cm^3 (preprocessing forced on) and 2.5 cm^3 at t=0.02 with 29-33 hulls. Exact-mesh overlap 0.81 cm^3.
sources.code: github.com/SarahWeiii/CoACD (MIT); pip coacd==1.0.11 = FlashCHORD's pin
sources.adoption_effort: Hours, CPU only. Replicate FlashCHORD's exact CoACD call (version, threshold, seed, preprocess mode) as an offline gate and run it on every library mesh plus every assembled or contact pose. No GPU.
sources.rule_risk: None. The tool runs on our own meshes. Changing CoACD parameters for the evaluation is likely not allowed (read from the checkpoint and evaluator), so control the mesh, not the decomposition.

sources.title: CRISP: Contact-Guided Real2Sim from Monocular Video with Planar Scene Primitives
sources.method: Fits about 50 compact convex planar primitives to the reconstructed point cloud by clustering depth, normals and flow, instead of simulating TSDF/marching-cubes meshes. Contact predicted from the human body completes support surfaces the human occludes (for example a chair seat). An RL humanoid tracker in simulation then checks the result.
sources.solves_for_us: Problems 1 and 2, and a general rule for 3. It is a published, measured case that TSDF meshes (over-smoothed surfaces, artefacts) break contact-rich RL tracking while planar primitives fix it. Our boards (and the dust-pan plate) are planar objects: refitting them as flat-faced, sharp-edged slabs with rectangular notches gives standing edges and CoACD-proof slots. Contact-guided completion is the analogue of using hands, table and other objects to complete what the cameras never saw.
sources.evidence: EMDB RL tracking success: TSDF meshes 75.9 %, NKSR 79.3 %, planar primitives 93.1 % (VideoMimic 44.8 %). Abstract: failure rate 55.2 % -> 6.9 %. Throughput 15K -> 23K FPS (+43 %). PROX non-penetration 0.925 (TSDF) vs 0.947 (planar). Missing small non-contact details were 'largely harmless', extra noisy geometry was not.
sources.code: github.com/Z1hanW/CRISP-Real2Sim and Z1hanW/holosoma-crisp (licence not checked)
sources.adoption_effort: We would not port their scene code. A planar or extrusion refit for the boards is about 0.5-1 day CPU: RANSAC the two large faces, fit the 2D outline in the board plane, extrude by the fitted thickness, cut notches from the interaction carve. Revolution refit for the cups and pot is another 0.5 day.
sources.rule_risk: Low. Hand-designed shape-class priors fitted to our own depth, with no GT and no generative model (CRISP's own pipeline uses MoGe/VLM contact priors, which we would not use). Document the prior.

sources.title: SPARCS: Simulation-Ready Cluttered Scene Estimation via Physics-aware Joint Shape and Pose Optimization
sources.method: Each object is a union of convex hulls whose vertices are optimisation variables along with the poses. An augmented-Lagrangian solve fits the point cloud (trimmed-ICP terms), keeps hulls collision-free with a twice-differentiable separating-plane contact model (SDRS), and enforces quasi-static force equilibrium (gravity, normal and friction forces). A 'separating-plane aggregation' regulariser makes occluded contact regions follow one common plane between two objects, which flattens unseen contact faces. SAM3D initialises the shapes; mass = 800 kg/m^3 x volume.
sources.solves_for_us: The closest published formulation to the owner's idea of building meshes from how the pieces interact. One optimisation removes penetration (ep24 overlap), floating (problem 3) and unsupported unseen geometry (problems 1 and 2, via equilibrium plus a planar contact interface). It works directly on the convex-hull representation the evaluator uses.
sources.evidence: MuJoCo, 5 tabletop scenes, up to 5 objects / 22 hulls. Max drift over 1 min: 0.73-3.10 cm (theirs) vs 31-173 cm (SAM3D+FoundationPose init). Max kinetic energy in the first second: 7e-4 to 1.1e-2 J vs 2.1-5.7 J. Converges in 6-9 ALM iterations, about 200-540 s per scene on CPU. Limitation stated: high compute; mass and friction set by hand.
sources.code: No code found (project page rory-weicheng.github.io/SPARCS has no repository link)
sources.adoption_effort: A full reimplementation (SDRS contact, structured solver) is weeks, so not feasible in 13 days. Feasible borrowings (1-2 days CPU): per-object-pair separating-plane flattening of unobserved contact regions, and a quasi-static equilibrium check as a gate.
sources.rule_risk: Their SAM3D initialisation is a pretrained generative prior (grey zone). We would start from our own TSDF instead. No GT.

sources.title: PhysPose: Refining 6D Object Poses with Physical Constraints
sources.method: Post-hoc optimisation of all object poses in a scene: pose cost (stay near the estimate, uncertainty-weighted) + collision cost (hinge on signed distance between CoACD parts of every object pair and the static scene) + gravity cost (hinge on positive distance of each part to the closest static support part along gravity, switched off when the object is supported by another). Analytic gradients. The table plane comes from RANSAC.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 3 (objects floating 1-4 cm and dropping at the start; residual object-object overlap) and part of 4. It is the principled version of our rest_settle: a per-frame (or rest-interval) pose refinement against the same CoACD parts the evaluator uses, with our measured table plane.
sources.evidence: YCB-Video AR: MegaPose 0.620 -> 0.707, FoundPose 0.690 -> 0.775. MSSD +0.13 (depth-sensitive) while MSPD barely changes. HOPE-Video 0.353 -> 0.395. Real Panda grasping: 0 % / 0 % / 60 % -> 80 % on 3 objects. Limitation: joint optimisation spreads errors from wrong detections or poses.
sources.code: No code found on the project page (data.ciirc.cvut.cz/public/projects/2025PhysPose)
sources.adoption_effort: About 1 day CPU. Our contact_retarget.py already has HullSDF (CoACD-piece signed distance) and the MuJoCo penetration probe. Add a gravity hinge for rest intervals and a pose prior; run per episode in minutes.
sources.rule_risk: None. Uses only our meshes, tracks, the table plane and gravity.

sources.title: Atlas3D: Physically Constrained Self-Supporting Text-to-3D for Simulation and Fabrication (with Make It Stand, SIGGRAPH 2013, as the classic balance formulation)
sources.method: Refines a mesh with: a standability loss (rotation deviation after a differentiable rigid-body simulation in Warp); a stable-equilibrium loss (the centre of mass must rise under small tilts, i.e. a potential well); and a Laplacian loss only on the bottom vertices below a height threshold (flat bases). Validated by forward simulation and by a perturbation protocol: random initial tilts up to phi_max, 13 angles x 100 trials per model. Make It Stand (Prevost et al. 2013) gives the static form: centre of mass over the support polygon.
sources.solves_for_us: Problems 1 and 2 (no stable standing pose; the sweeper's centre of mass 3 cm outside its footprint). In our setting it becomes a constraint on the unobserved region only: the perceived resting pose must be a stable equilibrium with a margin. Its perturbation protocol is a ready-made QA gate.
sources.evidence: Mean time-averaged rotation deviation reduced more than 6x vs Magic3D over 107 prompts. Stable-equilibrium loss raises success under perturbation. Stands on a 10 deg incline and on a sphere with friction. Cross-checked in an IPC simulator.
sources.code: Builds on NVIDIA Warp and threestudio; no Atlas3D repository link found
sources.adoption_effort: The differentiable-sim version is not needed. A non-differentiable search over the flattening depth and extent of unobserved bottom voxels plus static and perturbation settle tests in CPU MuJoCo: about 0.5 day.
sources.rule_risk: The SDS text-to-3D generator part is a generative prior and we would not use it. The stability losses and tests are fine.

sources.title: PhyRecon: Physically Plausible Neural Scene Reconstruction
sources.method: Neural SDF reconstruction trained with rendering losses plus a differentiable particle-based rigid simulator (DiffTaichi). Surface points come from a differentiable marching-cubes variant (SP-MC). The physical loss acts only on contact points (their motion during a drop onto the support). A 'physical uncertainty' grid accumulates where the object moves, which marks regions lacking support, and steers pixel sampling to thin structures. Stability is measured by drop tests in Isaac Gym.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 1 conceptually, and the QA gate. The physical-uncertainty idea transfers to our TSDF: voxels where a settle test shows rocking or rolling are the ones to complete, but only if they were never observed. Drop-test stability ratio as the acceptance metric.
sources.evidence: Stability ratio improves by at least 40 % over all baselines on ScanNet, ScanNet++ and Replica, with better chamfer distance and F-score. Thin structures (chair legs) recovered.
sources.code: phyrecon.github.io (repository not verified)
sources.adoption_effort: Do not port the neural pipeline. Borrowing the gate and the 'complete where unsupported AND unobserved' rule costs about 0.5 day.
sources.rule_risk: Uses monocular geometric priors (normal/depth networks); we would not. The gate idea has no risk.

sources.title: I2CD: Direct Image-to-Convex Decomposition for Simulation-Ready Collision Geometry (its simulation-readiness protocol)
sources.method: Predicts convex parts from one image with a frozen Hunyuan3D-2 model and a 38M-parameter head. The part we want is its evaluation: it defines 'asset preserved' as round-trip voxel IoU >= 0.9 between the geometry the engine actually collides with (hulls read back from MuJoCo, PyBullet, Genesis, PhysX) and the asset handed in, plus drop-and-settle tests in four engines.
sources.solves_for_us: The QA gate (owner's robustness question). 'It loads' is not 'it is right': MuJoCo, PyBullet and PhysX silently replace a dynamic mesh by its single convex hull. Our gate should read back what Newton/MuJoCo-Warp actually built from our mesh (the CoACD pieces) and compare it with our mesh, feature by feature (slots, rack gaps, cup interior).
sources.evidence: Raw generated meshes: 98 % had non-manifold edges and 2 % were watertight. The single auto-hull is the wrong shape for about 60 % of objects and keeps rocking on 16-21 % in MuJoCo/PyBullet. Clutter planning success: auto-hull 5/100, SAM3D+CoACD 90/100, I2CD 85/100.
sources.code: Not checked
sources.adoption_effort: Gate: about 0.5 day CPU (export Newton's built shapes or re-run the same CoACD, voxel IoU, per-feature overlap). The method itself is not needed.
sources.rule_risk: The method uses a pretrained generative prior (grey zone); the protocol does not.

sources.title: Newton collision pipeline: SDF mesh-mesh and hydroelastic contacts (with Factory, RSS 2022, as the SDF-contact precedent for tight-tolerance assembly)
sources.method: Newton can replace MuJoCo-Warp's contact generation (SolverMuJoCo(use_mujoco_contacts=False) plus newton.CollisionPipeline). Precomputed mesh SDFs (mesh.build_sdf(max_resolution or target_voxel_size, narrow band, margin)) give non-convex mesh-mesh contacts without convex decomposition; hydroelastic contacts need SDFs on both shapes. The docs say SolverMuJoCo's own pipeline collides a mesh's convex hull. Factory: voxel SDFs, per-triangle contacts and contact reduction simulate 1000 nut-and-bolt pairs in real time on one GPU.
sources.solves_for_us: Mainly a diagnostic for problem 2: an exact-geometry oracle to measure how much the CoACD hulls distort contacts (a board in a slot, a cup in the rack). It is not a fix for the evaluated score, because the official evaluator collides CoACD hulls and training with a different collision model than the evaluator is risky (see the poisoning entry).
sources.evidence: Factory: real-time 1000 simultaneous nut-and-bolt interactions. Its stated limitations are thin shells and low-tessellation flat surfaces (penetration on large flat faces). Newton docs: SDF path recommended over the BVH fallback; watertight meshes preferred.
sources.code: github.com/newton-physics/newton (Apache-2.0); Factory in Isaac Gym Envs / Isaac Lab
sources.adoption_effort: CPU settle-test oracle with Newton SDF: about 0.5-1 day. Training at 4096 worlds with SDF contacts is untested (memory and speed unknown) and not recommended.
sources.rule_risk: Changing the physics used in the evaluation is likely not allowed. Using SDF only offline for diagnostics carries no risk.

sources.title: Scalable Real2Sim: Physics-Aware Asset Generation via Robotic Pick-and-Place Setups
sources.method: A robot re-grasps each object in front of a static camera so every surface is seen (NeRF/GS with alpha-transparent training gives an object-only mesh). Collision geometry comes from convex decomposition (CoACD/V-HACD). Inertial parameters come from joint torques along an excitation trajectory, by convex optimisation with physical-consistency (pseudo-inertia positive-definite) constraints in Drake.
sources.solves_for_us: Partly problem 1 and the mass question. Its core fix for unseen undersides is to look at them (re-grasp), which we cannot do except where the episode itself shows the object lifted. That argues for fusing all lifted frames; our TSDF already does this when the underside is visible. Useful caveats: gaps and overlaps between convex pieces cause interior contact points and distort hydroelastic pressure. Physical-consistency checks on inertia are a gate.
sources.evidence: Mustard bottle (427.1 g): mass error 1.23 %, centre-of-mass error 6.33 %, rotational inertia error 358.6 %. 20-asset benchmark dataset released.
sources.code: github.com/nepfaff/scalable-real2sim
sources.adoption_effort: Robot-based identification does not apply. The pseudo-inertia check and volumetric inertia take about 1 h.
sources.rule_risk: None for the borrowed checks.

sources.title: Do as I Do (in-the-wild video to dexterous robot data; MuJoCo-Warp sampling retargeting)
sources.method: SAM3D meshes and SAM3D-guided tracking, then SPIDER-style annealed sampling in MuJoCo-Warp with warmup steps (the object is held while the hand settles). Per our earlier extraction from their code (docs/research/port-recipes-2026-10-21.md §2.2): CoACD hulls dilated by 2 mm, and a flat 'base plate' under objects that start in non-flat poses.
sources.solves_for_us: Precedent that others also patch physically invalid reconstructions with hacks (base plates, dilation) and with warmup. It does not solve our problem robustly: a plate the real scene does not have changes the evaluated physics.
sources.evidence: Retargeting success on 655 in-the-wild references: 25 % (SPIDER baseline) -> 71 %; warmup alone 0.66. OakInk2: 72 % -> 81 %.
sources.code: github.com/malik-group/do-as-i-do
sources.adoption_effort: Warmup or assist ideas are already covered by our curriculum work. The base plate costs about 1 h, if allowed at all.
sources.rule_risk: High for a base plate in the evaluated support USDA: a support the real scene does not have. SAM3D is a generative prior (grey zone).

sources.title: 'Your Robot Was Trained on a Lie': Collision Mesh Poisoning Attacks on Robotic Manipulation
sources.method: Deforms the collision mesh (a convex decomposition of a deformed copy) while keeping the visual mesh. Policies trained on the poisoned collision geometry are then evaluated on the benign geometry. The paper also argues that automatic convex decomposition is purely geometric and often fails to support an asset's intended interactions.
sources.solves_for_us: Evidence for one design rule: train and evaluate on the same collision geometry, and get that geometry right before training. A mismatch in collision geometry alone is catastrophic for a policy. This argues against SDF/hydroelastic training when the evaluation uses CoACD, and for gating meshes before any GPU run.
sources.evidence: Average drop of 56.09 percentage points in task success (Task 1, 9 YCB objects) when the collision geometry is restored to benign; 100 pp on Task 2; 26.32 pp on Task 3; real-world drop 61.67 pp over 3 objects.
sources.code: Not checked
sources.adoption_effort: None (a principle).
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: Digital-twin and digital-cousin real2sim family: RialTo, URDFormer, ACDC (digital cousins), ASID, Agentic Real2Sim
sources.method: RialTo (2403.03949): scanned digital twins plus inverse distillation. URDFormer (2405.11656): images to a URDF built from template parts. ACDC: retrieve similar assets from a library (cousins). ASID (2404.12308): active real-robot exploration to identify mass, friction and articulation. Agentic Real2Sim (2607.19190): VLM agents build a MuJoCo episode twin; a simulator-in-the-loop agent tries small object shifts and keeps a placement whose grasp succeeds; VLM mass hints.
sources.solves_for_us: Little. Asset retrieval or templates (ACDC, URDFormer) replace our reconstruction, and ASID needs real-robot interaction. Agentic Real2Sim's search over placements with the simulator in the loop is the same idea as our stable-pose snapping and rest settling.
sources.evidence: ACDC: 90 % vs 25 % zero-shot sim-to-real (cousins vs twin). RialTo: more than 67 % robustness gain. Agentic Real2Sim: 37-48/100 replay success over 4 VLM backends; sim-vs-real Pearson r=0.920 over 6 tasks; states it does not validate physical parameters.
sources.code: Mostly public (not checked individually)
sources.adoption_effort: Not recommended.
sources.rule_risk: High: retrieval or template assets break the own-mesh rule; VLM mass hints and generative meshes are grey zone.

ideas: H1 Planar refit of the boards, CoACD-proof (CRISP-style). Fit the two large faces by RANSAC, fit the 2D outline in the board plane, extrude by the fitted thickness with sharp edges, and cut rectangular notches whose width and depth come from the interaction carve (H3). Replace the TSDF board meshes with these. Supporting evidence: my measurement above (sharp edges keep the slot open, TSDF-like surfaces bridge it). Our boards' volumes (204 vs 324 cm^3) and smallest extents (3.05 / 2.66 cm, against mean thicknesses of 0.7 / 1.1 cm) suggest warped or over-thick reconstructions; that is a hypothesis. Falsification: (a) with FlashCHORD's exact CoACD, hull overlap at our ep24 assembled pose stays above 0.5 cm^3; or (b) the CPU settle test standing each board on its edge at the reference standing frames tilts more than 3 deg in 2 s; or (c) registered AUC of the refit boards on public episodes drops more than 0.01 against the current library (scans for diagnostics only); or (d) GPU A/B on ep24 (6 evaluations, about $4 per box) does not beat 0.31-0.32. If (a)-(c) pass but (d) fails, the limit is the policy, not the geometry.

H2 Replace 'flatten along one episode's up' with support-plane completion from every rest interval. For each interval where the object is static with no hand within 3 cm, put the table plane in the object frame. Remove unobserved material below it. Fill unobserved space between the lowest observed surface and the plane only inside the observed footprint's convex hull, then require the centre of mass over the footprint with a margin (Make It Stand / Atlas3D condition). Pool constraints over all public and eval frames of that episode's video. Falsification: on ep18 the generic rule does not recover the hand patch's footprint (11.7 cm^2 real; the patch reached SP/MP success at 0.715), or constraints from different rest poses conflict by more than 5 mm on observed surfaces, or settle tests on the dust pan, pot, pitcher and lid regress.

H3 Mutual-exclusion (interaction) carving. At frames where object B touches or interpenetrates A (assembled boards, cup in rack, lid on pot) and both poses are confident, set A's TSDF voxels to free inside B's observed-confidence volume (and vice versa). This generalises 'carve the slot from the overlap' to any object pair. Falsification: across the 12 two-object public episodes, the maximum exact-mesh overlap over all frames does not drop below 1 cm^3, or registered AUC drops more than 0.01, or the carved volume exceeds 10 % of the object's observed volume. The last would mean pose errors are over-carving, so carving must be limited to the best frames.

H4 PhysPose-style pose refinement of the references against the evaluator's CoACD pieces. Terms: a pose prior, hinge penetration against table, objects and hands, and a gravity hinge during rest intervals. It replaces rest_settle and removes the 1-4 cm floating (ep12, ep24, ep27). Falsification: after refinement, the rest-frame gap stays above 2 mm or penetration above 2 mm; or the reference's ADD against mocap on public episodes (diagnostic, after inference) gets worse by more than 2 mm mean. That would mean the heights were right and the underside geometry is wrong, so fix the mesh (H2) instead.

H5 A GT-free QA gate before any GPU spend, run on the exact evaluator collision. G1: engine round-trip voxel IoU of at least 0.9 between our mesh and the union of its CoACD pieces, plus per-feature checks (slot hull overlap under 0.5 cm^3, rack gaps open, cup interior open), following I2CD. G2: static settle at every perceived rest pose, under 3 deg and 5 mm drift in 2 s (SPARCS and Atlas3D style). G3: penetration audit, p95 under 2 mm. G4: floating audit, rest gap under 2 mm. G5: pair settle at contact poses (cup on rack tilt under 5 deg; boards in an X stay assembled). G6: perturbation test, ±5 deg x 50 trials, at least 90 % stand. Falsification: on our existing variants with known scores (ep27 0.91, ep12 0.79, ep18 0.345 before and 0.715 after the flattening, ep24 0.31), the gates fail to flag ep18-before, ep24 and the ep12 cup, or wrongly fail ep27 or ep18-after. Then the gates do not predict score and need new thresholds.

H6 The ep12 cup tips 23 deg because the rack's CoACD hulls bridge the wire gaps, or because our rack wires are too thick. At t=0.05 the tolerance is about 9-12 mm for a 30-40 cm rack, which is wider than typical wire spacing; that is an estimate. Test: G5 pair settle of the cup at our reference relative pose on (i) the exact rack mesh via Newton SDF and (ii) the CoACD hulls. If (i) holds and (ii) tips, refit the rack's wires as thin primitives. Falsified if both hold (then the tipping comes from the reference or from contacts) or both tip (then the mesh itself is wrong).

H7 Volumetric uniform-density mass properties (trimesh mass_properties on the watertight mesh, density about 800 kg/m^3 for wood and plastic as in SPARCS), instead of the surface-based centre of mass and inertia from make_assets, plus a pseudo-inertia positive-definite check (Scalable Real2Sim). Falsification: if surface and volumetric centres of mass differ by less than 3 mm for all 11 objects, drop the idea. Otherwise run G2/G6 settle tests under both and compare. Whether the evaluator honours our URDF inertial values is an open question for the organisers.

H8 Do not train with Newton SDF or hydroelastic contacts while the evaluator uses CoACD. The collision-poisoning paper reports drops of tens of percentage points from collision-geometry mismatch alone. Use SDF only as a CPU diagnostic oracle (H6). Falsification, if the owner wants it tested: a train-on-SDF, evaluate-on-CoACD A/B on ep27 (an easy episode) that matches the CoACD baseline. This is not recommended for spend.

H9 Revolution prior for the beige cup, blue cup, white pot, white pot lid and water pitcher (pitcher spout and handle stay as TSDF): fit an axis and profile and close the base with a flat disc. Falsification: no improvement in G2/G6 or in registered AUC on public episodes against library_v3 or v4, or AUC drops more than 0.01.
gaps: Whether the official evaluator uses our URDF mass and inertia and our support USDA. This decides whether mass properties or any support geometry are ours to set; ask the organisers.

The exact CoACD call inside FlashCHORD/Newton beyond threshold 0.05 (preprocess mode, resolution, merge, max hulls, seed). My test used coacd 1.0.11 defaults plus threshold 0.05 on synthetic boards. It must be repeated with the exact call on our real library meshes.

No published method reconstructs interlocking or slotted parts from observed interactions. SPARCS (static scenes, convex-hull shape variables, code not released) is the closest; H3 is our own extrapolation.
True board thickness and notch size are unknown at inference. The volume mismatch between our two boards (204 vs 324 cm^3) is unexplained; scans may only be used as public-episode diagnostics.

Physics-driven edits to unobserved geometry may lower the registered ADD-AUC (the score registers our mesh to the hidden scan). This must be measured on public episodes before adopting; no paper reports this trade-off for a registration-based metric.
Newton SDF/hydroelastic performance and memory at 4096 worlds is untested, and its usefulness is limited to diagnostics if the evaluator stays on CoACD.
Atlas3D and PhyRecon rely on differentiable simulation. Whether a non-differentiable search over unobserved voxels plus settle tests is enough is untested.

Gate thresholds (IoU 0.9, 3 deg / 5 mm drift, 2 mm penetration, 0.5 cm^3 slot overlap) are my guesses, borrowed loosely from I2CD, SPARCS and Atlas3D. They need calibration against our scored variants (H5).

Primary sources I could not open: Make It Stand full text (abstract and a community implementation only), the I2CD and poisoning paper code, and PhysPose code. The CoACD Table 1 numbers come from imperfect PDF text extraction.

verified.angle:
Fact-check of the "real2sim-collision" findings against the primary sources: CoACD (paper, README and C++/Python source at main), CRISP, SPARCS and PhysPose read in full from the arXiv HTML, with a spot-check of Atlas3D. WebFetch could not resolve arxiv.org, so the pages were downloaded with curl through the proxy. Text copies are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/factcheck_dl/. I ran one new CPU test with the colleague's own board generator, using coacd 1.0.11 with FlashCHORD's defaults (t=0.05, seed 0, pca off). Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/fc_scripts/seed_sweep.py, slot_rot_check.py and rot25_log.py in the same folder. No repository files were changed.

Main result: most of the quoted numbers are real. There are four material errors or omissions:
(1) SPARCS run time is 46-540 MINUTES per static scene, not 200-540 s.
(2) CRISP's 75.9/79.3/93.1 % is the combined success column, not EMDB. Its +43 % throughput is measured against VideoMimic (16K FPS), not against TSDF (15K).
(3) PhysPose's headline gains assume a known, ground-truth scene. With an estimated scene they are roughly halved.
(4) "Give CoACD a clean mesh and the slot stays open" is necessary but not sufficient. I measured a sharp limit: a gap survives the evaluator's CoACD only if its width w is greater than about 0.05 x L, where L is the longest axis-aligned bounding-box side of that collision mesh in the frame it is shipped in. The colleague's clean test sat only about 13 % above that limit, and rotating the same clean board 25 deg in its file collapsed it into a single hull.

checked.title: CoACD: Approximate Convex Decomposition for 3D Meshes with Collision-Aware Concavity and Tree Search (Wei et al., SIGGRAPH 2022) + README + source
checked.claim_checked: Concavity is measured on both the boundary and the interior. The mesh is cut with planes chosen by a tree search, with no voxelisation. About 20 vs 45 hulls against V-HACD on PartNet-Mobility. V-HACD fills toaster slots. The threshold equals t*L/1.6 metres. The default call is t=0.05 and seed 0. A clean notch stays open.
checked.verdict: confirmed for the paper and the source facts; partly for the conversion; the slot conclusion holds only conditionally
checked.what_source_actually_says:
Paper: concavity = max(Hb, k*Rv), with Hb a sampled boundary Hausdorff distance and Rv the radius of the volume difference (k=0.3 in config.h). It is computed after Normalize() scales the longest bbox side to 2.

Candidate cutting planes are AXIS-ALIGNED (xy/xz/yz), with optional PCA. The Python defaults are pca=False and seed=0 (main and the 1.0.11 copy in docs/research/work/19/coacd agree).

Table 1, PartNet-Mobility: V-HACD 44.6 vs CoACD 20.1 hulls, at CoACD threshold = V-HACD's concavity score (0.055 vs 0.052).

The paper says prior work fails by 'filling a toaster's slots'. HACD is the worst; V-HACD and Animation 'still suffer from the hole filling issues to some extent'. 'Stuff' is the colleague's paraphrase, not a quote.

Real-metric conversion (public/coacd.cpp, main.cpp): t_norm = t_real*2/L*0.8, so t*L/1.6 is the authors' conversion WITH a 0.8 safety factor. The geometric per-side tolerance implied by the cost is t*L/2, i.e. 5.75 mm for a 23 cm board, 3.7 mm for the 14.7 cm sweeper and 7.5-10 mm for a 30-40 cm rack.

README: -rm was added in 2026-04 and --split is recommended for engines that collapse a merged file into one hull. Licence MIT (LICENSE fetched). PyPI: 1.0.11 is dated 2026-05-04; the latest is 1.0.14 (2026-08-28).

MY MEASUREMENT (clean 23x13x1.2 cm board, notch from the top, exact FlashCHORD call, seeds 0-5):
- Aligned frame: W/L = 0.0543, 0.0565, 0.0696 and 0.087 kept 6/6 (3 hulls).
- Rotated 25 deg about (1,1,0): L grows 23.0 to 25.9 cm. W/L = 0.0483 gave ONE hull (slot filled) 6/6; W/L = 0.0503 filled 3/6; W = 1.6 and 2.0 cm kept but with 3-6 hulls.
- Rotations of 5-10 deg about the long axis leave L unchanged and change nothing.
