Objects with a hull-to-mesh volume ratio above 3 skip the penetration check. Every reference must also survive a 300-step simulator replay. The egocentric validation pipeline uses a SAM3D mesh from one reference frame, MoGe metric scale and FoundationPose tracking.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 2: the relative-pose reward targets exactly the assembled X relation between the two boards, and the containment relations (spoon in pot, cup in rack). It also gives organiser thresholds for reference quality checks (problem 4) and shows that the organisers' own video baseline relies on a generative mesh.
sources.evidence: 82.12% success on 1,831 benchmark tasks (reported earlier in our notes). The brush task from egocentric video reaches AUC 0.647 with a SAM3D mesh.
sources.code: Inside video_to_data / FlashCHORD (Apache-2.0).
sources.adoption_effort: Hours to check whether FlashCHORD exposes the relative reward for our two-object references. Then one GPU A/B per episode, about $3-4.
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: GATOR: Generative and Agentic 3D Object Reconstruction From Casual Images (NVIDIA LPR; Wu, Birchfield, Rabeti, Chang, Bowen Wen; arXiv 2610.11215)
sources.method: A multi-view generative reconstructor (patch-aligned RGB, target mask and pointmap features, mixed locally, plus text adapters) produces a complete, scene-posed asset. A multimodal agent then edits the mesh in Blender in an edit-render-review loop: it renders the original and the candidate under matched cameras, keeps edits supported by the input images and reverts the rest. Its instructions include 'use repetition and symmetry to complete justified hidden structure' and 'build supports from underside anchors'. It works within a 10-minute budget per object and has no access to reference meshes.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 1, partly problem 2. Bowen Wen, the organisers' reconstruction lead, states the issue directly: 'small geometric defects in supporting parts can make objects unstable'. His fix is an evidence-checked, general edit loop, not per-object patches. The pattern can be copied with our own agent (Claude), our depth, masks and tracks, and the drop test as the reviewer.
sources.evidence: Toys4K, four views: CD 0.009 vs 0.011 for Pixal3D-MV (-19.7%), F1 0.757 vs 0.701. On LM-O/HB/HANDAL tabletop scenes it has the best CD (0.009). In a PyBullet room with convex colliders, three generated chairs leaned or toppled before refinement and stood upright after it.
sources.code: 'Code (Coming Soon)' on the project page; the agent uses a proprietary model.
sources.adoption_effort: The code is not usable within 13 days. An idea-only port (agent proposes local edits to unknown voxels only, renders against our masks, then runs the drop test) is 1-2 days on CPU.
sources.rule_risk: The FAQ allows pretrained/generative models; the Kaggle rules require them to be publicly accessible at reasonable cost. Edits must stay confined to unobserved regions, so they cannot drift toward a 'remembered' scan.

sources.title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos (Malik/Abbeel group, UC Berkeley; arXiv 2606.19333)
sources.method: Builds a SAM 3D mesh, gravity-aligns it with GeoCalib, convex-decomposes it with CoACD and 'thickens and dilates object meshes by 2 mm to stabilise' contact-rich interaction. Retargeting is sampling-based MPC in MuJoCo Warp at 200 Hz (1024 samples x 32 iterations) with a penetration penalty of 3000 and random force perturbations. A warmup finds a stable initial state. Transition penalties fire for (1) no object-floor contact during reference rest timesteps and (2) no hand-object contact during in-hand timesteps.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 3 (drop at start, floating): the rest-contact penalty plus a warmed-up initial state. Problem 4: the dilation and penetration penalty. It is the closest group to us (Sharpa Wave hardware, MuJoCo Warp, CoACD).
sources.evidence: 71% vs 25% success for the baseline on reconstructed in-the-wild data. The authors write that 'the main differentiator is warmup, which discovers initial states that are much more stable and natural than the noisy initial frame'.
sources.code: github.com/malik-group/do-as-i-do (per our 2026-10-21 notes; licence not checked).
sources.adoption_effort: Rest-contact penalty as a FlashCHORD reward term: hours, plus one GPU A/B (about $3-4 per episode). Testing 2 mm dilation of collision meshes: minutes on CPU.
sources.rule_risk: None.

sources.title: SAM 3D: 3Dfy Anything in Images (SAM 3D Objects; Meta; arXiv 2511.16624, CVPR 2026)
sources.method: Single-image generative 3D (geometry, texture and layout) trained on about 3.14M untextured meshes with a human/model-in-the-loop pipeline. It completes occluded parts from learned priors. It is used for the object mesh by both the organisers' CHORD video pipeline and Do as I Do.
sources.solves_for_us: A fallback prior for the unseen underside (problem 1). It could be restricted to voxels that our TSDF marks unknown. It is unlikely to recover narrow notches (problem 2) that no frame shows.
sources.evidence: Our 2026-10-21 notes say its detail is coarse at arbitrary scale. No numbers were measured on our objects.
sources.code: facebook/sam-3d-objects (gated, 13.3 GB weights).
sources.adoption_effort: About 1 GPU-hour to set up plus about $2-5 to run on 11 objects. Needs scale alignment to our TSDF.
sources.rule_risk: Allowed by the FAQ (pretrained model, publicly accessible after the gate). The organisers' own baseline uses it.

sources.title: Newton adds contact-rich manipulation: SDF collision and hydroelastic contact (NVIDIA Technical Blog, 16 Mar 2026)
sources.method: Newton's collision pipeline can bypass MuJoCo Warp's native point contacts. It supports SDF collision directly on non-convex triangle meshes and hydroelastic pressure-patch contact: set ShapeFlags.HYDROELASTIC and create a CollisionPipeline with an sdf_hydroelastic_config. Skild uses it for connector insertion.
sources.solves_for_us: In principle, slot-in-slot contact for the boards (problem 2) without convex decomposition. In practice the official evaluator builds objects as CoACD hulls (scene/eval.yaml: decompose_objects true, CoACD threshold default 0.05), so the slot must exist in our mesh and survive CoACD.
sources.evidence: Vendor claims; no numbers for our use case.
sources.code: Newton (open source). FlashCHORD pins Newton 1.2.0.
sources.adoption_effort: Not for eval; at most an offline cross-check of mesh contact.
sources.rule_risk: The evaluator's physics is fixed; changing it would invalidate submissions.

sources.title: Video2Sim2Real: Full-Stack Autonomous Dexterous Skill Acquisition from a Single Human Video (arXiv 2606.08828)
sources.method: Builds a digital twin from an RGB-D frame: Gemini scene parsing (objects plus material labels), SAM3 masks, SAM 3D Objects meshes. Each mesh is canonicalised and shifted 'so that its lowest point lies on the support plane'; mass and inertia come from mesh volume times a material density; friction and restitution come from a material table. Grasps are filtered to avoid points within a band above the lowest point.
sources.solves_for_us: Problem 3, but only with the same lowest-point-on-plane heuristic we already use. Nothing for stability or slots. The mass-from-volume x material rule could replace the default 0.3 kg if mass matters for tipping.
sources.evidence: Improved simulated success over baselines on several everyday tasks; no asset-level metrics.
sources.code: Not checked.
sources.adoption_effort: Hours (heuristic only).
sources.rule_risk: None (a VLM material label is a pretrained model, which the FAQ allows).

sources.title: AGILE: Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction from Video via Agentic Generation (SIGGRAPH 2026; arXiv 2602.04672)
sources.method: A VLM-guided generative model produces a complete, watertight, textured mesh regardless of occlusion. The pose is anchored at the interaction-onset frame and propagated, avoiding SfM. A contact-aware optimisation adds an interaction-stability loss (hand and object move rigidly together during a grasp) and SDF non-penetration. Results are retargeted to a Shadow hand in Isaac Gym.
sources.solves_for_us: Shows that a watertight generative mesh plus a non-penetration loss gives sim-usable hand-held objects (problem 4). It has no support or stability term, so it does not address problems 1-3.
sources.evidence: Claims 100% sequence success vs prior methods failing on up to 75% of complex sequences (HO3D/DexYCB/ARCTIC). Real-to-sim retargeting is shown only qualitatively.
sources.code: Project page agile-hoi.github.io; code status unknown.
sources.adoption_effort: Days; not worth it within 13 days.
sources.rule_risk: Generative prior, allowed by the FAQ.

sources.title: Combinative Matching for Geometric Shape Assembly (ICCV 2025 Highlight; arXiv 2508.09780)
sources.method: Models interlocking parts by two properties, 'identical surface shape' and 'opposite volume occupancy', and learns correspondences where surfaces match but the volumes fill inverted space.
sources.solves_for_us: Grounds problem 2 in a principle, not a fix: in an assembled or contained state, one part's volume marks the other part's empty space (notch, rack slot, pot interior). That is the basis for the mutual-exclusion carving idea below.
sources.evidence: Beats the prior state of the art on geometric-assembly benchmarks; geometry only, no video.
sources.code: Project page linked from arXiv; not checked.
sources.adoption_effort: Use the principle only.
sources.rule_risk: None.

ideas: Stage 0, prioritise by eval exposure. The kit roster has 36 pairs: wooden_spoon 10, pot 6, blue_cup 5, rack 5, beige_cup 2, sweeper 2, dustpan 2, and 1 each for lid, pitcher and the two boards. Containment contacts are spoon/cup/pot/sweeper with the rack (eval 14, 15, 16, 28, 30), spoon in pot (3, 5, 6) and lid on pot (1). A general fix for cavities and support therefore reaches about 10 eval episodes; the board-slot fix reaches only eval 25. Falsify the ordering: if a CPU physics gate (Stage 3) on our eval references flags no rack, pot or spoon episode, the cavity work drops in priority.

Stage 1a, 'support closure' replaces per-episode flattening (hypothesis). Detect rest segments automatically with the organisers' still-run rule: under 1 mm and under 0.01 rad per frame, at least 5 frames, fingertips more than 2 cm away. Map each episode's table plane into the object frame. Carve everything below the plane, and mark unknown voxels inside the object's vertical silhouette column above it as solid (visual-hull closure). Also stop table-pixel rays from carving within about 1 cm of the footprint; grazing rays are a likely cause of the rounded base. The evidence comes from every episode in which the object rests, with no per-object code. Falsified if any of these happens on the 11 library objects: an object fails the organiser-criteria drop test from any observed rest pose (CoACD hulls, tilt at most 15 degrees, support within 2 cm, settle within 2 degrees); mean CD-O against the public scans (diagnostic only) worsens by more than 0.05 cm; or ep18 registered AUC falls below the hand-flattened v3 (0.715).

Stage 1b, mutual-exclusion carving (hypothesis). Two rigid bodies cannot overlap. For each co-tracked pair, transform B's current mesh into A's frame at every confidently tracked frame (with a 1-2 mm margin) and mark it as free space for A. Alternate A and B for 2-3 rounds; hands and the table already carve. This one rule should open the board notches, the rack slots and the pot interior. Falsified if any of these holds: ep24 CoACD-hull overlap in the assembled pose does not drop from 13.5 cm^3 to under 0.5 cm^3; the ep12 cup still tilts more than 5 degrees after a 2 s objects-only settle in the rack (now 23 degrees); or rack/pot/board CD-O worsens by more than 0.05 cm. The last would mean tracking error is carving away real material; then restrict carving to frames whose depth residual is below a threshold.

Stage 1c, generative completion only where no constraint reaches (hypothesis). Run SAM 3D, which the FAQ allows and the organisers' baseline uses. Scale-align it to our TSDF and import its geometry only into voxels that are still unknown after 1a and 1b, never overriding observed surface. Falsified if CD-O and drop-test pass rate on the 11 public objects do not beat 1a+1b alone.

Stage 2, feature-preserving meshing for planar parts (hypothesis). The rounded board edges come from 4 mm voxels plus Gaussian smoothing. Detect dominant planes with RANSAC on the fused surface, snap vertices within 3 mm to them and reduce smoothing; for slabs, alternatively extrude the fitted 2D outline including the carved notch. Falsified if a board still has no stable on-edge pose (drop test from on-edge, tilt at most 15 degrees) or board CD-O rises above 0.25 cm. Check that the packer's advisory 'box-like' MESH WARNING does not fire.

Stage 2b, check that the evaluator's collision geometry keeps the slot (hypothesis). Eval uses decompose_objects true with CoACD at its default threshold of 0.05 on whatever mesh we submit. Hypothesis: that keeps a notch of about 1.3 cm wide and about 7 cm deep open. Falsified if the partner board penetrates the hull union by more than 2 mm in the assembled pose. In that case the slotted mesh alone will not fix ep24/eval 25; test 2 mm dilation (as in Do as I Do) or a pre-split mesh.

Stage 3, a physics acceptance gate as automatic CPU CI on every mesh and reference, built from organiser criteria. (a) Drop test from each detected rest pose. (b) CHORD-style hand-object and hand-hand penetration at most 2 cm (ours is already tighter). (c) Object-object hull penetration at most 2 mm at every frame. (d) Object-support gap at most 5 mm at rest frames. (e) A 300-step replay without NaNs. It needs no ground truth, so it runs on eval episodes too. Falsified as a predictor if, on the public episodes with GPU results (ep12, 18, 24, 27 and the earlier batches), gate failures do not go with lower registered AUC (for example Spearman below 0.3).

Stage 4, decide floating versus pedestal from evidence rather than by habit. On public episodes only (ground truth used as a diagnostic after inference), compare our reference object height at rest frames with mocap height, after the scorer's registration. If our object sits above ground truth by about the float, the error is in the pose: settle it down onto the table (current rest_settle). If our height matches ground truth, the mesh bottom is missing: fix the mesh (Stage 1a), or add an organiser-style support disk at the object's minimum z (support_recon.py, phantom filter for objects resting on objects). Falsified if neither rule reduces rest-frame MPPE on ep12/24/27.

Stage 5, policy-side terms for inter-object relations. Add CHORD's relative object-pose reward for the two-object contact episodes and Do as I Do's rest-contact transition penalty (no object-floor contact during reference rest frames). Run on ep24 with slotted meshes, with and without the reward, 6 evaluations each, about $7-8. Falsified if registered AUC improves by less than 0.03 over slotted meshes alone.

Benchmark choice and a rule question (hypothesis about the hidden reference). SoySauceChicken's CD-O of 0.065 is below the floor that even a budget-decimated perfect scan reaches against a full-resolution reference (at least about 0.15 when weighted by eval exposure). So either the hidden references are stored at the 4096 budget and their meshes nearly equal the public scans, or something else about the reference is unknown. Hypothesis: hidden references are budgeted. Falsified if the organisers state they use full-resolution scans. Practical consequence: treat Zihao Guo (AUC 0.831, SP-SR 0.95, CD-O 0.313) as the own-mesh bar. Have the owner ask the organisers whether public-scan meshes for eval objects are penalised; the FAQ only says 'should'.

CD-O quick win on hollow and thin-walled objects. Our worst CD-O values are on beige cup (0.87), pitcher (0.88), rack (0.57) and blue cup (0.52), which together cover 13 of 36 eval pairs. Hypothesis: their interiors are filled or their walls thickened by TSDF 'fill' closure. Carving the interior that is seen through the opening, plus mutual exclusion with spoon and cup, should bring each below 0.40 cm. Falsified if a rebuilt mesh does not drop below 0.40 cm against the public scan, or if the drop test from the rest pose then fails.
gaps: I found no technical report, code, Discord post or paper by SoySauceChicken, Zihao Guo (hideinpoopoo) or SRL on meshes or physics. GitHub search is blocked in this session and web search returned nothing. Danyang Yan's only paper (arXiv 2607.22434, shadow expression with a dexterous hand) concerns collision-aware hand-pose search, not object assets.
The resolution and format of the hidden reference scans are undocumented. My inference that SoySauceChicken (0.065) and Kiarash (0.088) submit scan-identical meshes depends on it.

It is unclear whether the organisers or judges would accept per-object support disks (pedestals) in Track 3 references. The evaluator loads any Cylinder or Cube prims from our support USDA, and the organisers use the same mechanism for the CHORD benchmark data, but no Track 3 statement exists.
Untested: whether the evaluator's default CoACD threshold (0.05) keeps a narrow board notch, rack slots or the pot interior open. Our meshes have not had the slot yet, so this has never been checked.
GATOR code is 'coming soon' and its agent uses a proprietary model; AGILE code status is unknown. Neither can be adopted within 13 days except as ideas.
The wooden spoon (10 of 36 eval pairs) has no public scan, so we cannot measure its CD-O or shape error; its physical validity (thin handle, contact with pot and rack) is unmeasured.

NVIDIA Cosmos: I found no asset-generation or physics-validation tool relevant to rigid object meshes; Cosmos Reason is only a possible VLM judge. Newton's SDF and hydroelastic contact cannot be used inside the fixed evaluator.

The organisers' Isaac Sim drop test is not validated on RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120) according to the repo README. A faithful port to MuJoCo or Newton on CPU may differ in contact details from the evaluator's MJWarp plus CoACD path.

The mass is recorded as 'assumed_grounding_default'. Quotes: 'never falls back to a geometry-derived pose'; 'Convex-hull stable-pose ranking is intentionally out of scope'; 'A failed standing test ... does not pass the batch job'. In explicit_colliders.py a non-watertight CoACD part is replaced by its convex hull (CoACD threshold 0.05, at most 16 hulls, at most 64 vertices per hull). The visual or shape mesh is never edited, so 'never repairs geometry' holds at shape level. (2) When the target mesh differs from the sequence mesh, the tool does not use the sequence poses. It re-tracks the target mesh with multi-view FoundationPose over the first 90 frames, using RGB, depth and masks. (3) It assumes the object begins the recording resting on the ground or another horizontal support, and handles one rigid object only, with no object-object support. (4) The drop is a kinematic lift of 0.25 x the largest extent, then a release. That is harsher than the evaluator's frame-0 start. Important correction: the colleague says our rest_settle snap matches their principle. It does not. rest_settle (pipeline/contact_retarget.py, stable_ups plus max_tilt=15) rotates the object's reference pose onto the nearest convex-hull stable face, which is exactly the geometry-derived pose the official tool refuses. The robust form is the reverse: keep the observed rest pose, require the mesh to stand there, and repair the mesh if it does not, the way flatten_base did for ep18. checked.claim_checked: 82.12% success on 1,831 tasks. VOC wrench at scale 1.0 for a 20-step warm-up after a random-frame reset. Relative object-pose reward for two-object tasks. checked.verdict: confirmed (but the relative reward is not in FlashCHORD)
checked.what_source_actually_says:
Abstract: '4,739 bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks ... Evaluated on 1,831 benchmark tasks, CHORD achieves an average success rate of 82.12%', and 90.77% for whole-body tasks.

PDF appendix: 'The per-environment virtual object-control scale is reset to 1.0, followed by a 20-step warm-up period before applying the curriculum target.' The relative reward is gated by m(t), active only during object-object interaction phases, as an exponential kernel over the inter-object pose error.

Quality check: the hand is modelled as capsules against the object's convex hull, with analytic capsule-capsule hand-hand overlap. A sequence is rejected if either overlap exceeds 2 cm in any frame. Objects with a hull/mesh volume ratio above 3 are excluded from the hand-object check. The replay runs 300 steps in Isaac Lab.

Egocentric validation: one brush task. Grounding DINO plus SAM2 for masks, SAM3D mesh from the reference frame, metric scale by registration to MoGe depth, FoundationPose tracking, ViPE plus Dyn-HaMR for the hand, then a Gaussian-splat joint refinement. They 'report 0.647 AUC'.

Code check: the Isaac Lab path (robotic_grounding/tasks/v2d/mdp/rewards.py) implements relative_object_pose_reward with pos_sigma 0.05 m, rot_sigma 0.5 rad and a proximity gate. FlashCHORD at 7eb9721 has no relative term: objectives/ and configs/objective/tracking.yaml list keypoints, joints, contact_wrench_support, missed/unintended contact, termination and force_closure only.
checked.code_status: Apache-2.0 inside video_to_data. The relative reward exists only in the Isaac Lab trainer; porting it to FlashCHORD (JAX) is real code work, not a config flag.
checked.applicability: Do not expect the relative reward to fix ep24. With our board meshes overlapping by 13.5 cm^3 at the assembled pose, the target relative pose cannot be reached physically, so no reward can make the policy reach it. Fix geometry first, then A/B the relative reward. Its broader value is that it targets RPE directly on all 16 two-object eval episodes. The quality-filter thresholds (2 cm capsule-vs-hull, 300-step replay) are useful organiser-sanctioned gates for our references; our contact retargeting already beats 2 cm (p95 2.7-6.0 mm). The 0.647 AUC is a single task with a single-view generative mesh. It is a floor for the organisers' own video pipeline, not a benchmark.

checked.title: GATOR: Generative and Agentic 3D Object Reconstruction From Casual Images (Wu, Birchfield, Rabeti, Chang, Wen; arXiv 2610.11215, 8 Oct 2026)
checked.claim_checked: Generator conditioned on multi-view RGB, mask and pointmap, plus text, then a Blender edit-render-review agent. Agent instructions on symmetry and repetition and 'build supports from underside anchors'. 10-minute budget, no access to references. Toys4K 4-view CD 0.009 vs 0.011 (-19.7%), F1 0.757 vs 0.701. Chairs toppled before refinement and stood after it in PyBullet. 'Code coming soon'. Proprietary agent. Quote attributed to Bowen Wen.
checked.verdict: confirmed numbers; characterisation needs correction
checked.what_source_actually_says:
The numbers match: 'reducing CD by 19.7% and raising F1 from 0.701 to 0.757 relative to ... Pixal3D-MV'. The agent is GPT-6-Astra, run through the Codex CLI with extra-high reasoning effort, under a ten-minute budget. It 'has no access to reference meshes'.

Appendix D.6: 'small geometric defects in supporting parts can make objects unstable'. The test is 15 objects in a ScanNet++ room in PyBullet with convex colliders and an assumed mass; three chairs lean or topple before refinement and stay upright after it. This is qualitative, essentially n=3. The sentence is a co-authored appendix line; Wen is last author and submitter, not its sole voice.

Corrections:
(1) Refinement edits are local and 'only slightly worsens CD, F1, and IoU on HANDAL'. It helps simulation, not chamfer.
(2) There is no physics or geometric check in the loop. Review is the agent comparing renders, and the limitations section lists 'automatic geometric verification of agent edits' as future work.
(3) The prompt forbids 'floor-snap', 'closure of functional holes' and 'flattening whole components to hide damage'. It asks to 'Infer occluded external structure from ... repetition, symmetry and simple construction priors'.
(4) The paper reports 'Agentic refinement recovers regular holes and slots that the generative model variants leave irregular or missing'.
checked.code_status: The project page shows 'Code (Coming Soon)'; no licence. The agent depends on a proprietary model.
checked.applicability: Nothing usable before the ~2026-11-04 freeze. The transferable pattern: an edit loop confined to unobserved regions, checked against our own masks and depth, with a physics gate added by us. The 'drop test as reviewer' step is our hypothesis, not GATOR's method. Falsifier: on public episodes, edited meshes must pass the gate AND must not raise CD-O against the public scans (diagnostic use only). Their slot-reopening result is the closest published evidence that narrow functional gaps are a known failure of generative and fused reconstructions (ep24). Their 'no floor-snap' rule is a caution against blanket base-flattening of objects that do not rest on a flat face.

checked.title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos (Paliwal, Etukuru, Liang, Abbeel, Shafiullah, Malik; arXiv 2606.19333, 17 Jun 2026)
checked.claim_checked: SAM 3D mesh, GeoCalib gravity alignment, CoACD, 2 mm thicken and dilate. Sampling MPC in MuJoCo Warp at 200 Hz with 1024 samples x 32 iterations, penetration penalty 3000, random force perturbation. Sharpa hand.
checked.verdict: confirmed
checked.what_source_actually_says: Appendix: 'MuJoCo Warp simulator, with a simulation timestep duration of 0.005s (200 Hz). We convex decompose object meshes using CoACD, and to stabilize hand-object interactions ... we thicken and dilate the object meshes by 2mm.' Planning runs every 0.5 s over a 3 s horizon, with 1024 samples and 32 iterations; Table 4 has penetration_penalty_scale 3000.0. The trajectory is aligned with gravity using GeoCalib. The robot is the 22-DoF Sharpa Wave. On reconstructed in-the-wild data they reach 71% success vs a 25% baseline. 'The main differentiator is warmup, which discovers initial states that are much more stable and natural than the noisy initial frame.' For real deployment they align the initial z and yaw manually.
checked.code_status: Released: github.com/malik-group/do-as-i-do, MIT licence (LICENSE fetched). It contains reconstruction/, retargeting/ (CoACD decomposition plus MuJoCo Warp MPC, sharpa default) and deployment/. The GitHub API was blocked for this session; I read the README, retargeting/README and LICENSE via raw.githubusercontent.
checked.applicability: (1) Their warmup result supports Problem 3: settle the initial scene in simulation and start from a stable state rather than the noisy first frame. Our reference sets frame 0, so this is in our control. (2) The 2 mm dilation stabilises contact but works against Problems 2 and 3: it adds 2 mm of float and 2 mm to the ep24 overlap. Using a dilated collider while submitting the undilated mesh is a grey area under 'a pose must place the submitted mesh correctly in the simulator'; flag it before trying. (3) It does nothing for standing or slots.

corrected_ideas: Replace rest_settle's pose snapping with a mesh-side fix plus a gate. The official tool fixes the orientation from the observed rest window and refuses geometry-derived poses. Our snap to the nearest convex-hull stable pose (up to 15 degrees) edits the scored trajectory. Robust order: observed rest pose (fixed), then mesh must stand at it, then repair the mesh in unobserved regions only. Falsify on public episodes: if the snapped variants score higher registered AUC than flattened-mesh variants at the observed pose, keep the snap.

Gate stage 1, single object (ported from mesh_to_usd, CPU MuJoCo, the same CoACD hulls at threshold 0.05 as the evaluator). For every rest window we observe (not only the first 90 frames): a zero-lift settle, which is what the evaluator does at frame 0, and the official 0.25 x extent lift-drop. Pass if tilt is 15 degrees or less, support is within 2 cm, and the pose settles within 1% of extent (clamped to 1-10 mm) and 2 degrees. The support must be the surface actually under the object (table OR the other object's mesh: lid on pot, cup in rack). The official tool only handles the ground plane.

Gate stage 2, object pairs (our addition; the official tool is single-object). At every frame where two tracked objects are within a few mm, compute the hull-vs-hull penetration depth and volume (ep24 is 13.5 cm^3 today). A reference fails if the overlap exceeds a few mm, since no policy can reach that state. Apply this to all 16 two-object eval episodes, not 12. The colleague missed ep8 cup+pot, ep10 cup+cup, ep32 and ep33 cup+spoon, so container and nesting relations matter even more.

Repair stage A, plane contact: replace per-episode flattening with a fused support constraint per object. Collect the up vectors from every observed rest window in every public and eval episode of that object (our tracks only). Cluster them. Add a planar contact patch only on surfaces that were never observed and that face the plane in a consistent cluster. Respect GATOR's caution: do not flatten objects whose observed rest contact is not planar.

Repair stage B, interaction carving, generalising the slot fix: carve voxels of object A that object B's tracked volume occupies in at least k frames with good tracking. Cap the carve depth and require that the carved region was unobserved, or observed as free space, in A's own views. Falsify on public ep24: the carved boards must bring the assembled-pose overlap near 0 AND must not raise CD-O against the public scans (diagnostic only). Second hypothesis to test first, cheaply on CPU: even with slots in the mesh, FlashCHORD's CoACD (threshold 0.05, no hull cap) may bridge a narrow notch. Decompose a slotted board and measure the hull overlap at the assembled pose. If the notch is bridged, lower the CoACD threshold for the boards in our scene config, which the evaluator honours because it rebuilds from the checkpoint config.

Floating objects (Problem 3): first measure whether the 1-4 cm float is a tracking z bias. Take the object-bottom-to-table gap at our rest windows; mocap may be used on public episodes as a diagnostic only. If it is a consistent bias, correct it in tracking or the mesh (a resting object touches the plane under it) instead of adding support_recon pedestals, which keep the scored error. Pedestals are a disclosed fallback only. Note the 1-4 cm float already exceeds the 2 cm support tolerance of the official standing check.

Relative reward: it is in CHORD's paper and the Isaac Lab code (pos_sigma 5 cm, rot_sigma 0.5 rad, proximity-gated) but absent from FlashCHORD at 7eb9721, so it means a JAX port. Do it only after the pair gate passes. Its payoff is RPE across 16 eval episodes, not ep24 alone. A/B on public two-object episodes with registered AUC and RPE over at least 6 repeats.

CD-O: the hidden references are proven to be at most 4096 vertices and faces (the scorer's row-ID merge plus the 294,912-row sample). The 0.15 floor argument is moot. Own-mesh teams with credible CD-O sit at 0.24-0.31 (SRL, Zihao Guo); ours is about 0.50. The biggest weighted contributors are rack (5 pairs, 0.572), blue_cup (5, 0.520), pot (6, 0.444) and beige_cup (2, 0.868). Treat 'leader used public scans' as unverified; solidSF.com, NVSimranPatil and Panav Raaj are also at or below 0.112.

Generative completion (GATOR-style) is not available before the freeze (code coming soon, proprietary agent). The FAQ allows pretrained models, so an open single-image or multi-view generator such as SAM 3D, which both CHORD and Do as I Do use, is a legitimate prior for unseen undersides. Gate any generated geometry the same way. Falsify by CD-O against the public scans and by the physics gate on public episodes before touching eval.
